items.body:
The brotherhood of foundational European avant garde bassists gets smaller with each passing year. And among those still living, some are either inactive for various reasons or working in other fields, musical or otherwise. So, the subset of ones still going is a small but precious list.

Among them is the Netherlands’ Arjen Gorter. Ask even a relatively informed listener of European avant garde jazz about him and almost invariably the first association will be Willem Breuker, and more specifically his Kollektief. Gorter did anchor that group for the entirety of its existence (1975-2010, with a retrospective farewell tour coming after Breuker’s death) alongside drummer Rob Verdurmen, allowing Breuker and a rotating cast of string and horn players (though trombonist Bernard Hunnekink was another stalwart) to navigate complex and subversive music, confident that a strong foundation would always support them. But like Jimmy Cobb always being referenced first and sometimes only as the last living participant of Kind of Blue after Miles Davis died in 1991, Gorter’s career, still ongoing, is hardly exclusive to his work with Breuker.

Gorter was born in Amsterdam on January 2nd, 1948 and he has resided in the Dutch capital his whole life. His road to the bass was a circuitous one. As he wrote in an email, “I liked the accordion when I was very young. It was common in the Amsterdam streets of the ‘50s, but the tunes that my teacher made me play were too silly, so that did not last. My dad imported musical instruments. He brought a slightly damaged ukulele home and so at around 11 I tried playing along with the nightly jazz broadcasts on French and Belgian radio. The father of a friend had a small jazz collection and I loved the Art Blakey Blue Note 45s, the Monk LP and the other stuff he had. So that ukulele was replaced by a guitar. I started jamming in our attic with friends and others and at some point someone brought a double bass upstairs and left it there for six months. I had fun playing it and managed to buy it from him once he showed up again.”

During high school Gorter played guitar in a band for school dances, repertoire ranging from period rock tunes to jazz compositions. He began college in 1966, aiming to study political science and sociology, the same year he first worked professionally with Breuker, having heard the older reed player’s bands around town and once playing with him at a jam session. Gorter was invited to join a new Breuker group, which performed at the Loosdrecht Jazz Competition as a sextet, then expanded to almost two-dozen musicians for the final stage. This group would make Litany for the 14th of June 1966 (Relax) in late October 1966, Gorter’s recording debut alongside two other bassists, the much older Dick van der Capellen and Victor Kaihatu.

Gorter would balance university and performing for a few years. During this time, he would work with Germany’s Gunter Hampel, appearing on his April 1968 Wergo date Gunter Hampel Group + Jeanne Lee and participating in the November 1968 Total Music Meeting in Berlin, where photo evidence has him in a bizarre encounter with Hampel, John McLaughlin, Sonny Sharrock, Pharoah Sanders, Roy Ayers, Laurie Allan, and Roel Kroes. 1969 saw even more activity: more Hampel work, including the album The 8th of July 1969 (inaugurating his Birth imprint); playing on German trumpeter Manfred Schoof’s FMP release European Echoes and being part of the Peter Brötzmann Oktett at the International Holy Hill Jazz Meeting (alongside Buschi Niebergall and Peter Kowald; Richard Williams’ review of European Echoes in the March 14th, 1970 issue of Melody Maker saying, “It’s an astonishingly powerful performance, with particularly superb work by Dudek, Bailey and the three basses, who play a really fantastic trio section.”). Gorter is also heard on the Live at The Bohemia Jazzclub recording by Hans Dulfer’s Soulbrass Inc., as well as a track with Breuker and Han and Peter Bennink heard on the Instant Composers Pool cheese box. As Gorter recalled, “I managed to juggle both activities until the end of 1969, but I was more on the road than in Amsterdam and had to make a choice and I chose the activity that gave me way more satisfaction.”

During the first half of the ‘70s, Gorter and Breuker did not work together often, at least as can be gleaned from available recordings: Hampel’s People Symphony (Birth, 1970) and part of his group that participated in German avant garde composer Hans Werner Henze’s Der Langwierige Weg In Die Wohnung Der Natascha Ungeheuer; and an unofficial Amsterdam recording from 1973 under Breuker’s leadership and a live date from Leo Cuypers in 1974, both with groups prefiguring the Kollektief (Cuypers was its first pianist). Otherwise Gorter was busy – again, at least on record – with Hans Dulfer, Kees Hazevoet, Theo Loevendie, Alexander Von Schlippenbach, and the Irène Schweizer-Rüdiger Carl Quartet. The latter two were significant. Gorter was part of the second iteration of Schlippenbach’s Globe Unity Orchestra, Niebergall and Kowald in tow once more (a 1970 Berlin Jazz Festival performance released in 2001) and the Schweizer-Rüdiger Carl group that was active for several years. “I met Rudiger in Wuppertal, that was a new jazz center by itself thanks to Peter Brötzmann and Peter Kowald,” wrote Gorter. “Sometimes I stayed at the studio that he shared with guitar wizard Hans Reichel. When Irene and Rudiger started playing together, they asked me to join and we played many places in the early ‘70s, with Heinrich Hock, Louis Moholo, or Alan Bateman on drums.” That band made only one full album, 1974’s Goose Pannée (FMP) but did have a track on the For Example - Workshop Freie Musik 1969 - 1978, the FMP boxed set.

1974-75 was an important period for two other reasons. Besides the aforementioned collaborations as well as work with the Boy Edgar Big Band and the small groups of Maurice Horsthuis and Toon van Vliet, Gorter was one of the musicians who helped establish Amsterdam’s Bimhuis, ultimately one of Europe’s premier venues for avant garde music, performing on its October 1st, 1974 opening night with the Burton Greene Quartet. Then in March 1975, Breuker asked Gorter to be a member of his Kollektief. Gorter described the group’s music as such: “Willem’s music had a lot of freedom. There were often tightly arranged written sections that would suddenly end and then the fun was to play on as if the arrangement continued – there was usually no such thing as chord changes – or to let the thing fall off a cliff ... Anyway, the music always felt fresh to play, even after many concerts, and there was a great mix of individual input and group discipline and cooperation. The Kollektief’s music linked the recognizable to the unexpected, often in 90-degree turns. It was surprising but accessible. For us musicians there was a wide spectrum of activities, from theater plays to movie music to interpretations of classical music and a lot of traveling to places where we found appreciative audiences, ranging from Australian school children to Chinese businessmen.”

The Kollektief would go on to make over three dozen albums, mostly released on Breuker’s BV Haast label, and perform all over the world, including during the Klap op de Vuurpijl (roughly, Top It All Off) Festival, taking place over five days at the end of each year from 1976-2005. Its book mixed Breuker and other band member pieces with tunes from various pages of the Great American Songbook and drawn from the classical canon, as well as other sources, presented in a highly theatrical manner best appreciated live and mixing in humor in refreshing contrast to the dour stage demeanor of many an improviser.

As busy as the Kollektief would keep him, Gorter still pursued other projects, some including fellow Kollektief members, including Breuker, and only existing on stages, such as groups under the leadership of Maarten van Norden, Sean Bergin, Boy Raaymakers, Pierre Courbois, Nedly Elstak, Jasper van ‘t Hof, Misha Mengelberg, and others. A representative sampling of those can be found in the archive of the Bimhuis (https://www.bimhuis.nl/archief); when he was in Amsterdam, this would be Gorter’s home near his home.

But there were also ones documented as albums: Maine, the 1975 collaboration of American trombonist Roswell Rudd with Dulfer, Gorter, and drummer Martin van Duynhoven, was made up of music by Sonny Rollins and Rudd (who had been coming to and working in the Netherlands since the mid ‘60s both with the New York Art Quartet and also locals like Loevendie). There were two 1977 dates by Cuypers, Zeeland Suite also including another bassist in South African expatriate Harry Miller; the 1979 Maarten Van Norden/Boy Raaymakers quartet date Chicken Song, completed by drummer Peter Nykyruj (of Mike Osborne fame); and a pair of 1980 albums spearheaded by the aforementioned trumpeter/composer Elstak (and released on his Coreco label; Gorter had loosely studied harmony with him in the ‘60s): To Build was led by Soesja Citroen’s name, who was one of five singers alongside Elstak, Breuker, Gorter, and Van Duynhoven for Sad Trumpets. The most significant, at least in terms of international exposure, came in July 1984, when Gorter, Mengelberg, and Bennink joined forces with two Americans, soprano saxophonist Steve Lacy and trombonist George Lewis, for the Soul Note release Change of Season (Music Of Herbie Nichols). Another important recording came 13 years later with Legendary: The 27th of May 1997, in a reunion with Hampel, who was fêting his seminal Heartplants SABA album from 1965 with original participants Courbois, Schlippenbach, and Schoof, Gorter standing in for his late friend Buschi Niebergall. One interesting takeaway from this is that it is often thought that after Breuker split with his fellow Instant Composers Pool founders Mengelberg and Bennink there were two distinct worlds in Dutch avant garde jazz; however, there were musicians like Gorter who operated in both spheres.

The new millennium found Gorter in several new projects: the mostly American blues/jazz band New Texas Swing from American saxophonist and then fellow Kollektief member Alex Coke with singer Tina Marsh and drummer John Betsch; the aptly named though horn-heavy Drummers Double Bill from Arend Niks and Verdurmen; 2000 recording The Compositions Of Eric Dolphy (BV Haast) with Coke, Breuker, Eric Vloeimans, Frank van Bommel, and John Engels; and Bo Van De Graaf’s I Compani; and the Rahsaan Roland Kirk “tribute” band Reeds & Deeds, also put together by Van De Graaf.

The Dolphy project had a personal resonance for Gorter, more specifically a much younger version of himself. In 1964, when he was 16, Gorter attended the Charles Mingus Sextet performance at Amsterdam’s Concertgebouw, a band with Dolphy, Johnny Coles, Clifford Jordan, Jaki Byard, and Dannie Richmond, which Gorter calls “the best ever ... Halfway through a trumpet solo by Johnny Coles, Eric left the stage while playing and walked into the hall. He ended up right next to my seat, way in the back. For a 16-year-old, that may have been a life-changing experience.” In 2011, Gorter was given the opportunity to celebrate Dolphy once more with a concert at the Bimhuis: “Eric Dolphy at The Five Spot Revisited,” with the legendary recording’s repertoire played by himself, Tom Arthurs, Rudi Mahall/Alex Coke (as his bass clarinet and saxophone/flute sides), Benoît Delbecq, and John Betsch.

Gorter joined the multimedia ensemble I Compani, founded by Van De Graaf in 1985, in 2010. As he wrote, “Bo van de Graaf just called it quits for I Compani, which I understand but regret. He led that band for 40 years through great adventures and I was happy to participate since 2010 or so. If anyone is comparable to Breuker in the amount of initiatives he took, it is him. Original pieces are blended with film music and live video, in various lineups from septet to 18-piece band. His music has the space, freedom and versatility of Breuker’s, but in a different way. Fun!”

When asked about the European scene in which he came up, Gorter replied, “At that time every European city had a very original and recognizable improvised music scene, or a few of them, like London with both the Spontaneous Music Ensemble and Brotherhood of Breath,” he wrote. “And they all had international contacts and were sharing with each other. So, the originality of these approaches, and the mutual respect, encouraged the exchange between countries and scenes and the musicians and their supporters took the initiative to made it happen.”

As for his own methodology towards, as shown in this piece, the variety of musical situations in which he has taken part, Gorter spoke both simply and profoundly: “From the beginning I played both free improvisation and tunes based on chord changes. Learning on stage was an option in the ‘60s, which sometimes led to embarrassment but more often to improvement. My approach is: first try to play what you hear, then figure out what others call it (= music theory), then apply that to play better what you hear and so on. Nowadays much education starts on the second step ...”
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦荷兰低音提琴手Arjen Gorter的专辑与生涯回顾。他于1948年生于阿姆斯特丹，1966年首次与Willem Breuker合作并录制首张专辑，早期经历涵盖手风琴、尤克里里、吉他直至低音提琴。其音乐根基深植于欧洲先锋爵士传统，与Breuker Kollektief的合作长达数十年，为乐队提供稳固的低音支撑。乐评将Gorter置于欧洲先锋爵士贝斯手的谱系中讨论，强调其个人创作生涯不应被与Breuker的合作所遮蔽。文字带有浓厚的历史文献性质，记录了1960年代荷兰即兴场景的生态与人物网络，对了解欧洲先锋爵士发展脉络具有参考价值。

items.body:
There is a substantial list of attributes that sets Ran Blake apart from every other innovative pianist of the past sixty-plus years, each of which falls under one of two headings: his choice of materials and his treatments of them. The former is based on Blake’s ability to hear connections between materials for which “disparate” is an inadequate descriptor. Who else would sequence Max Roach’s “Mendacity” and “Saving All My Love for You” – or “On Top of Old Smokey” and Michel Legrand’s “Watch What Happens”? Nobody, because what Blake does is unique. He doesn’t interpret materials as much as administer an MRI, revealing the connective tissues and vital organs as vividly, if not more so, than the skeletal structure. In the process, Blake makes the familiar sound radically new.

Blake’s collaborations with singers are central to his work. The current critical consensus is that his groundbreaking work with Jeanne Lee overshadows everything since, the respective qualities of notables like Christine Correa and Sara Serpa notwithstanding. Roots & Byways circumvents the edifice The Newest Sound Around has become, primarily because Dominique Eade takes a different tact. She is not as rooted as Correa – or Lee, for that matter – in Billie Holiday, and she is not as committed to understatement as Serpa. Like both Correa and Serpa, Eade can shape a song syllable by syllable and render a highly personal interpretation. It is Eade’s palpably deep joy in singing that sets her apart, one that is not only bursting at the seams on showstoppers like the Whitney Houston megahit, but one that even seeps into noirish songs like Mingus’ “Portrait.” It is the key to her relatability and appeal, and to that of the album, as well.
items.label: Sunnyside SCS 1813
items._cn_summary: 钢琴家Ran Blake与歌手Dominique Eade合作的专辑展现出极为独特的选曲逻辑——将Max Roach的硬波普作品与Burt Bacharach的抒情经典并置，或在民谣旋律旁安置Michel Legrand的电影配乐。Blake并非传统意义上的诠释者，更像是对素材进行深层扫描的诊断者，揭示出不同曲目之间隐藏的肌理与器官。Eade的演唱延续了Blake与声乐合作者（如Jeanne Lee、Christine Correa）一脉相承的逐音节雕琢传统，但她的路径不同：既不像Correa与Lee那样根植于Billie Holiday的传统，也不像Serpa那样执着于克制，反而以歌唱中可感知的深层喜悦为核心特征——这种特质在Whitney Houston式的爆款金曲与Charles Mingus的暗色调作品《肖像》中均有流露，构成专辑情感张力的关键来源。整体而言，这是一张在选曲美学与演唱取径上都带有鲜明个人印记的声乐爵士作品。

items.excerpt: ‘What the Fog’ is the second outing for the collaborative pairing of David Allred and Peter Broderick. items.body: ‘What the Fog’ is the second outing for the collaborative pairing of David Allred and Peter Broderick. The compositions on the 45-minute release from the Dauw label extracted from a soundtrack to an 11-hour documentary called #monalisa that shows a day in the life of the Louvre in Paris as people engage in art, crowds, and technology – and in that order. The film feels like a balance of recognising the disconnect that exists between those engaging in art in a commercial space – a disconnect that seems further exasperated when technology adds another layer of removal. But it is also a recognition of those quiet, shared moments of human connection because of, and sometimes in spite of the art, that seemingly gives the space its meaning. Musically, Allred and Broderick are up to the task of elevating the narrative and emotional are of that lived experience. ‘What the Fog’ Begins with an ending. An almost mournful one at that. Where the film feels like a proper opening, slowly easing us into its world, the music feels like it could just as equally be an outro. “The Foghorn” opens with digital ether and then a trumpet enters, playing out like a military sendoff in a way. There’s a sort of lamenting to these early notes. Slowly, washes of distortion undulate beneath it all, letting the trumpet melody drift away. But, as piano enters, an inviting calm and reflection begins to take hold. And when the trumpet rejoins the piano, this time the piece feels more ruddered. Second piece “Cloud clearing” is bright and brief. Broderick’s lilting piano work invites us to stay in that place of calm a little further. “Stasis Oasis” sounds like it’s title – rutted and lumbering. But this contrast with piece 2 shows how Allred and Broderick can quickly strike to the heart of a moment and immerse the listener. The piece teases a tension between optimism and defeat. “Sky Swamp” undulates with slow piano strikes, over a haze of ethereal electronics. Piano chords play in slow motion creating suspense throughout – like an emotional metronome, measuring feeling at a few bpm. The synths flower above, as if waiting for the signal to shift or decay. “Crystal Flower” returns to some of the tones of “Oasis Stasis”. Eventually, vapour trails of trumpet float by in the background as sci-fi like sounds whiz by – almost alluding the dystopian dynamics of a crowd immersed in personal technology rather than communal art. Sonically, the piece feels like a new layer to the overall composition. And the once mournful trumpet seems more vivacious almost ready to transform, but it is buried in the background as if trying to fight its way through the mirage of technological decay. “Deep Dark” is as murky as it sounds. Deep in darkness with barely a shred of light. It’s feeling almost all consuming. “Shadow Diver” opens in a circulating wash of distortion. As piano and trumpet enter, hope returns. But it moves at a slow pace as if exhausted by all that has come before. Drums enter, settling into a groove – but it’s a haunted one that provides a sense of progress in the face of exhaustion. Closer “Outer Lands” with slow swaths of synths – the album is never afraid to play with and tease sci-fi tropes. But as it unfolds, it evolves into a piano-driven piece. And by the end, there is nothing but a lone piano to end things. It’s bittersweet – cautiously hopeful but somehow exhausted from the journey. All totaled, “What the Fog” comes in around 45 minutes – a snap shot of the larger film. But as a contained narrative unto itself, it tells a full story with a beginning, a middle, and an end. It’s an evocative journey with layers that will keep the listener coming back, likely more immersed on each return. What The Fog by Allred & Broderick www.dauw.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Peter Broderick与David Allred合作的第二作，源自为卢浮宫一日纪录片《#monalisa》所作的配乐，约45分钟。评论指出影片试图捕捉艺术商业空间中人与艺术之间既疏离又偶发联结的张力，而音乐恰好承担了提升这一情感与叙事弧线的功能。作品以数字氛围与小号开场，呈现出近似送葬的哀悼感；钢琴进入后情绪转为宁静沉思。其后各曲在慢速钢琴、合成器雾气、失真洗刷与小号之间游走，曲目标题如"Cloud clearing"、"Stasis Oasis"、"Sky Swamp"暗示静态、悬置与张力。整体呈现出一种缓慢推进的冥想质感，电子处理与现代作曲手法并存，并以小号作为人声般的情感载体贯穿始终。

items.body: A sea without a port “Life springs from death, just like the sun rises each morning after its nightly voyage to the heavenly plain.” Anyone who knows Joseph Sannicandro from his work on A Closer Listen, will know that he’s not someone who will take anything at face value, but likes to dig around and uncover the background stories behind any releases he might be writing about, outlining motivations and socio-political connections, which allow him to draw up illuminating interviews with artists. He’s seldom off duty and when he goes off to Mexico City (or el DF) he takes his digital recorder with him, much in the same way that a XIX traveller might’ve carried a sketchbook jotting things down, taking notes, outlining the aural world he encounters in a bid to unpack its complexities. And yet he is wise enough to recognise himself as an American tourist with all the cumbersome baggage that comes with it. In the extensive linear notes to A Sea Without A Port, Sannicandro states, “As our southern neighbor, there is the uncomfortable fact that so much of what is now the USA was once Mexico, the forgotten/repressed/unknown fact that much of the Mexican-American war was fought because Mexico had outlawed slavery. The fact that European settlement was forced on the indigenous peoples. Bigots and TV pundits cultivate fear of ‘illegal’ immigrants, yet ironically Mexico has long been perceived as a place where American ruffians and outlaws could flee to escape justice.” It follows that one of the tracks is titled “El tratado de Guadalupe” denying any possibility that this could ever be interpreted as a picture postcard rendition of DF. However, Sannicandro is neither descriptive nor dogmatic in his approach. “The post-colonial Mexico, the Mexico rocked by the effects of NAFTA, of sprawling slums and terrible poverty, of colonized peoples and traditional ways of life obliterated by the violence of multinational corporations and agricultural subsidies” are all acknowledged but never color our listening experience. Rather, it’s cultural filters that are used to ease our way into the complex sonic territory. The opening track, “I dreamt I was dreaming and I came home too late,” is titled after poetry by Roberto Bolaño. Aside from friends and musical connections (Umor Rex), Sannicandro is quick in paying tribute to the work of Juan Villoro, Leon Trotsky, Frida Kahlo, Francis Alÿs, Alejandro González Iñárritu, Octavio Paz, Rufino Tamayo and all the artists and writers who introduced him to DF long before he physically set foot there. And yet A Sea Without a Port never feels like the result of thoroughly researched homework. It is never dry, on the contrary, it sizzles with stimuli. Sannicandro is not interested in adopting an observational stance. He happily tampers with field recordings preferring the textural to the documentary. He clearly has fun with whatever is picked up by both his Tascam DR-05 and his iPhone 3GS and is unafraid to compromise the supposed integrity of the untreated material. Presumably, in order not to be overwhelmed by the task at hand, he breaks down any possible linear narrative into disjointed chapters, often opting for jump cuts rather than cross fades. He’s constantly revising, retracing lines, rubbing out and filling in the gaps with new contradictory aural impressions, abruptly stopping the flow of sound almost mid sentence to introduce startling pauses. Chubby Cheker’s Let’s Twist Again filters through the fuzzy sonic ambience of the title track, snippets of lines from popular TV dramas populate “Ivan Illich”, short tape loops of street hawking play over and over like broken records on “Non-aerial cartography”, reverb blasts through “A halo is antiquated”. Everything is fragmented, shaken up and eventually blended to produce an intoxicating auditory mixture extracted from the city’s nooks and crannies. Over the last 20 seconds of the last track, “The tragic concision of the dream”, Sannicandro introduces another snippet of what could be perceived as quintessentially “traditional Mexican music” but frustrates any expectations one might have of finally having time to savour its melodic quality by unceremoniously dropping the tune after only 10 seconds or so, leaving us with nothing to hold onto, and the impossibility of grasping yet again the “characteristic Mexican spirit” of his chosen location. As Sannicandro explains, “These recordings acknowledge the impossibility of ever truly knowing a place, especially one as rich and complex and contradictory as el DF.” A Sea Without a Port is out as free digital download on Galaverna. a sea without a port by Joseph Sannicandro www.noiseeconomy.wordpress.com www.soundcloud.com/thenewobjective
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以墨西哥城为创作背景，融合实地录音与电子声响处理，将田野采风的城市声音作为素材来源。作者明确避免以旁观者姿态进行纯粹记录，而是对这些声音进行质地化的重新塑造，呈现出后殖民语境下墨西哥城的历史与文化张力。专辑以波拉尼奥诗句作为引子，并在多首作品中融入对《瓜达卢佩条约》、NAFTA影响等政治历史议题的隐晦回应。评论者强调作者在创作中游走于观察与主观介入之间，让田野录音不成为文献式的记录，而是成为带有文化过滤与个人感知的声景构建。整体而言，这是一张将旅行笔记、历史反思与声音实验交织的作品。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由斯洛伐克小提琴家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，汇聚Spectrum Quartett弦乐四重奏、Nogaband传统弦乐组合及Ulijanky女声合唱团，将斯洛伐克民间音乐的素材与二十世纪古典作曲家的作品重新对接。曲目主要取材自Eugen Suchoň、Ilja Zeljenka、Alexander Moyzes及Bartók等斯洛伐克与匈牙利作曲家的创作，每首作品的民间源头——采集地与演奏者——均在注释中标注。编曲摒弃管弦乐式的圆润处理，保留了民间音乐的粗犷能量与原生声乐质感。演奏与演唱者深谙传统音乐的语汇，呈现出一种根植于民间土壤的当代演绎，既是对古典与民间割裂传统的修复，也是两种传统的深度对话。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦俄罗斯占领区约两万乌克兰儿童被强制带离家园的战争罪行，以音乐为媒介呼吁关注。乌克兰-加拿大歌手Marichka联合两国音乐人完成录音，编制以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉琴、钢琴与罕见的双陶笛（由曾被绑架后成功归国的16岁少女Lisa独奏演绎）。曲目融合传统民歌与原创，主题沉重却以克制手法呈现：首曲《Foreign Land》以祖辈被迫离家务工的传统旋律映射当代被夺走的儿童，演唱温柔内敛；次曲《Rusalka》则由Alina Kuzma领唱，取材于斯拉夫民间传说中的田野与河流精灵，音乐风格骤然转为激烈粗粝。专辑在传统女性吟唱的基础上加入当代叙事张力，使古老民歌体裁承载了迫切的政治与人道主义诉求。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的新专辑《The Gods Laugh》延续了她一贯的模糊风格边界，将民谣、前卫音乐与宗教氛围融为一体。核心乐器为中提琴、管风琴、击弦古钢琴与钢琴，并加入鼓、贝斯与合成器扩展音域。多数作品为单次即兴录制，呈现出一种近乎神秘的低语感，仿佛穿越时光而来。《I Am!》以 John Clare 的诗作为词，叠加恒定嗡鸣与超脱旋律；《Sprigs of Heather》开篇致敬中世纪圣咏，随后转为钢琴主导的缓慢级进，凝练而精致。专辑也是对 Cotton 已故父亲的纪念，《The Final Harvest》记录父亲最后一次前往心爱菜园的旅程，充满难以言喻的温柔。光与暗在音乐中交织渗透，情绪不断流转，最终成为独属于 Alison Cotton 的声音。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这是挪威Camilla Hole Trio的专辑《Langs》，相比前作《Eventyrferd》中科幻合成器与传统素材的大胆结合，本专辑显得更为脚踏实地，但仍延续了对本国传统音乐的探索。主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，爵士影响贯穿始终，同时融入挪威西部民间舞蹈音乐元素。乐队成员角色不固定，人声旋律、低音和鼓点之间频繁交换主导位置，开篇曲《Springleik》中加入了模块合成器与颤音琴的叠加音色，即兴段落充满流动性。整体呈现出北欧爵士与民间音乐融合的实验气质，乐手之间的互动方式灵活开放，传统曲调被置于自由即兴的框架中重新诠释。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，共五首曲目。由北欧民谣界经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，乐手各自带入不同视角诠释传统曲目。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的奔跑节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；《Nordgård》由成员Morten Musicus原创，引入口弦和风笛形成持续的推进力。传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》加入洋琴作为精致背景；终曲《Orms》作为纯器乐曲，由口簧、长笛和弦乐交织，制造出令人兴奋且略带失衡的声响质感。整体弥漫着古老、质朴的氛围，乐器组合与传统北欧民谣的呈现方式展现出乐队成熟而精湛的功力。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 音乐厅完成两小时无脚本独奏即兴，录音后混入稀疏的人声采样、打击乐、循环音轨、田野录音与拾得声响，形成专辑《Sendas》。Sosa 师承塞隆尼斯·蒙克的「不重复」理念，拒绝被归类于爵士、拉丁或古典任何标签，强调首遍即兴的自然流露与「少即是多」的减法美学。作品植根于加勒比与拉丁传统，同时拥抱自由即兴与声音实验，带有冥想色彩与低频共鸣意识。文末摘录的访谈呈现其独立姿态——对抗算法分类与流媒体工业逻辑，追求与听众共同踏入未知。评论在技术细节处戛然而止，但已充分勾勒出一张关于孤独创作、即兴哲思与跨文化融合的专辑轮廓。

items.body:
GUEST COLUMN
NO. 341
カサンドラ・ウィルソンへの追悼
Cassandra Wilson 1955–2026
2026年9月19日
ゲスト・ コントリビューター

カサンドラ・ウィルソンの訃報に接し、1990年代にニューヨークで彼女に会ったときの、あの圧倒的な存在感が蘇った。それは、決して威圧するような存在感ではなかった。そこには、まるでミシシッピーの大地のような大らかさと、深い優しさがあった。そして、涅色のドレッドヘアーの美しい女性だった。その人間性が、美しさが、そのまま彼女のボーカルに現れていたのだと思う。

カサンドラ・ウィルソンの登場は、JAZZボーカルにおける新たな革命だった。彼女が現れたときの衝撃を、私は今でも忘れられない。深く豊かなコントラルトの声、独特の呼吸、音の間に生まれる静寂、そしてビートにわずかに後ろから寄り添うようなレイドバックしたフレージング。声量や技巧を前面に押し出すのではなく、一つひとつの音を深く響かせ、歌わない「間」までも音楽にしてしまう。その歌唱には、楽器奏者の即興にも通じる自由さがあった。

私が彼女に早くから注目していたのは、1980年代のニューヨークで、アルトサックス奏者スティーヴ・コールマンを中心とするM-Baseの新しい音楽活動に参加していた時代からである。既成のジャズの形式に安住するのではなく、新しいリズム、新しいハーモニー、新しい音楽言語を模索するその環境の中で、カサンドラ・ウィルソンの声は、単にバンドの上に乗る「ボーカル」ではなく、一つの楽器として音楽そのものを構成していた。そこには、後に世界的なディーバとなる彼女の革新性が、すでにはっきりと現れていた。

そして彼女の凄さは、ジャズというジャンルの中だけでは語ることができない。ブルース、フォーク、ポップス、ロック、カントリー、R&Bなど、さまざまな音楽を取り込みながら、彼女は決してそれらを借り物のスタイルとして歌わなかった。どのような曲であっても、カサンドラ・ウィルソンが歌えば、それはカサンドラ・ウィルソンの歌になってしまう。曲のジャンルや既存のイメージを超えて、自分自身の声、自分自身の呼吸、自分自身の感性によって、まったく新しい音楽へと昇華してしまうのである。

そこには、単なる歌唱技術を超えた、ボーカリストとしての本質的な力があった。メロディーを正確に歌うこと、音程をコントロールすること、豊かな声を持つこと。それだけでは、人の心を深く動かす歌にはならない。カサンドラ・ウィルソンには、その人がどのような人間なのかというものが、声そのものに現れていた。ニューヨークで感じたあのおおらかさ、優しさ、そして大地のような深さ。それが彼女の一音一音に宿っていたからこそ、彼女の歌には、技術だけでは説明できない説得力があったのだと思う。

偉大なボーカリストは、曲を歌う。しかし、さらに稀有なボーカリストは、曲そのものの存在を変えてしまう。カサンドラ・ウィルソンは、その領域に達していた。誰もが知っている曲であっても、彼女が歌った瞬間、そこにはそれまでとは違う景色が現れる。旋律、言葉、リズム、呼吸、沈黙。そのすべてを自分の身体の中に取り込み、もう一度、自分自身の音楽として生み出す。だから彼女の歌を聴くと、「この曲をカサンドラ・ウィルソンが歌っている」のではなく、「これはカサンドラ・ウィルソンの歌なのだ」と感じるのである。

2026年、カサンドラ・ウィルソンは70歳でこの世を去った。1955年生まれの彼女と、1956年生まれの私は、ほぼ同じ時代を生きてきた。これまでの人生と経験、そして培ってきた表現のすべてが結実し、まさにアーティストとしての集大成へ向かう時期だったはずだ。それだけに、あまりにも早い別れが、無念でならない。そして今、私は彼女の最高傑作「New Moon Daughter」を聴いている。

合掌。

Ptof. 稲吉紘実   Prof.Hiromi Inayoshi

Prof.稲吉紘実は、あらゆるデザイン・芸術分野のエキスパートであり、唯一無二の総合芸術家である。特にマーク・ロゴデザインの第一人者として、世界を代表するCIデザイナーの一人である。デザインを芸術へと昇華した「象徴芸術」という新たな芸術分野を確立。デザインのアカデミー賞、New York ADC賞で世界初のゴールドメダル2冠を同時受賞するなど、国内外で100を超えるデザイン賞を受賞。2026年には世界3大デザイン賞の一つ、iF DESIGN AWARD 2026を受賞した。近年は音楽監督として、NYでジャズやオペラのプロデュースを行う。また、ジョン・コルトレーンの「私は聖者になりたい」という言葉により、社会・平和活動を世界各国で展開し、「世界一大きな絵」や「Love Earth Love Children World Art and Music Aid」など、芸術と音楽の偉大な力で世界を変えることをミッションとしている。その活動は国連で「博愛の象徴：稲吉紘実の世界展」が開催されるなど、世界的な評価を得ている。

items.body: “Yira Ye” takes its title from a Bambara phrase that means roughly “that’s how it is”, and it is the first single from L’Ombre du Croco, the debut album  Bamako Express release through Trad Records on 30 October. The Ghent quartet pairs two Belgian folk players, violinist Anouk Sanczuk and guitarist Florian De Schepper, with Malian balafonist and singer Joël Massa Diarra and Burkinabè percussionist Ousmane Dembélé on djembe and calabash. Their songs are sung in Bambara. Over the past year they have played concert stages and the balfolk nights of Flanders, where couples dance to live folk bands, and in 2026 they won Best Live Band at the Flanders Folk Awards. At a balfolk night the violin carries the tune for the dancers, and in Mande music the balafon does much the same job; “Yira Ye” passes the melody between the two over Dembélé’s djembe. The track moves from quiet melodic passages into full dance rhythm, and De Schepper steps forward for a guitar solo, recorded with the rest of the song by Jeroen Geerinck at Studio Trad. Stream and listen to “Yira Ye” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Bamako Express – Yira Ye appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: 比利时根特四重奏 Bamako Express 将欧洲民俗乐手与马里和布基纳法索传统演奏者结合，以班巴拉语演唱。这首单曲是首张专辑的首发作品，通过小提琴与巴拉风之间的旋律交接构建跨文化对话，同时以金贝鼓和葫芦 percussion 推动舞蹈节奏。歌曲从安静的旋律段落逐步展开进入完整舞曲节奏，并包含一段吉他独奏。整体制作由 Studio Trad 完成录音。虽然乐队获得了弗拉芒民俗奖最佳现场乐队，但音乐本身更偏向传统世界融合方向，缺乏明显的实验性或前卫元素。传统乐器的运用和非洲与欧洲民谣的结合具有一定文化深度，但创新空间有限，适合民俗与世界音乐爱好者。

items.body: Ghost Reflection, the dark electro and industrial project of Alexander Borsov, releases the concept album “Dark Triad” digitally on Aliens Production. The eight-track record mixes melodic lines, IDM loops and analog electronics around a horror-themed narrative. Borsov wrote, produced, designed and mastered “Dark Triad” himself. Aliens Production describes the record as “a cinematic concept rooted in horror aesthetics and rhythmic themes.” The tracklist runs “Games of psychopaths,” “Dark Triad,” “Integration of Madness,” “Infected,” “The root of evil,” “Thorny path,” “The Shattered World of Illusions” and “Order of Darkness.” Dark Triad by Ghost Reflection Ghost Reflection’s ‘Dark Triad’ concept The eight tracks move from “Games of psychopaths” through “Integration of Madness” and “The root of evil” to the closing “Order of Darkness,” a sequence built around horror imagery and rhythmic industrial and IDM production rather than a conventional song structure. “Dark Triad” first appeared under Borsov’s own Bandcamp page in September 2025 and now returns through Aliens Production as a digital release. About Ghost Reflection Ghost Reflection is one of several recording names used by Slovak producer Alexander Borsov, alongside Dark the Keeper, Darkmechanic and Stellar Dynamics, all mixing electro-industrial, noise and horror-themed dark electro elements. Borsov is also a member of the group Diverje and got his start in metal bands including Morgue, Atom, Cremation Deads, Sarcoma and Satura before moving into electronic production. Under the Ghost Reflection name, Borsov released the album “Dark Thinker” in June 2022 and the single “Dark Noise” in February 2024. “Dark Triad” followed in September 2025 and is now released digitally through Aliens Production, the Slovak dark electronics label that has operated since 1997 and hosts a roster of industrial, dark electro and EBM-adjacent acts.
items._cn_summary: 斯洛伐克制作人Alexander Borsov以Ghost Reflection名义发行概念专辑《Dark Triad》，由Slovak独立厂牌Aliens Production数字发行。整张专辑围绕恐怖美学展开叙事，八首作品从"Games of psychopaths"逐步推进至"Order of Darkness"，旋律线与IDM循环交替运作，配合模拟电子音效构建出连贯的暗色工业图景。Borsov独自完成创作、制作、设计与母带处理，体现出独立制作的高度自主性。其音乐背景跨越金属乐队时期与当前电子制作领域，将electro-industrial、噪音与黑暗电子元素熔于一炉。专辑结构偏向氛围化的概念叙事而非传统歌曲架构，节奏工业与IDM元素作为骨架贯穿始终。作为一张信息性较强的专辑发布介绍，文章并未深入探讨具体的声响创新或制作细节，但勾勒出了一位多产独立电子制作人的创作脉络。

items._cn_summary: 冈比亚音乐家Suntou Susso延续西非格里奥传统，以科拉琴为核心乐器展开创作。专辑标题《Jaliya Silokang——格里奥之路》直接点明其传承意图，将世代口述的历史记忆融入琴弦律动之中。作品根植于曼丁哥文化的叙事脉络，通过传统琴音构建跨越时空的听觉场景。在保留科拉琴原始韵味的基础上，探索格里奥这一概念在当代语境下的表达可能。专辑由独立厂牌发行，体现了非主流音乐地区的艺术自主性。整体偏向传统世界音乐范畴，对熟悉西非音乐语汇的听众具有特殊吸引力，但与实验性或前卫音乐的融合空间相对有限。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于北马其顿地下独立音乐场景的长篇报道节选，而非具体专辑评论。作者Jakub Knera是中东欧地下音乐领域的资深撰稿人，其系列文章聚焦被主流忽视的左翼音乐生态。文中重点介绍了Gostivar的'Sepak Se Vrti'音乐节，以及在马其顿音乐基础设施极度匮乏的条件下坚持运作35年的地下电台Stotrojka。通过Janevski等核心人物的视角，揭示了一个充满韧性、在系统缝隙中蓬勃生长的独立音乐社群。这篇文章适合对中东欧非主流音乐景观、地下文化生态感兴趣的读者，从中可了解到北马其顿独立音乐的脉络与生存状态，以及电台、节庆等非商业载体如何维系当地音乐创造力。原文信息有限，未涉及具体音乐作品的声音分析。

items.body: Archie Forde hails a compilation of young Icelandic electronic music makers, austere experimentalists and noisemongers, which rails against gentrification and foreclosed futures alike safn by plata It’s October 2025, and Icelandic noise music collective Spider Network are crammed into a Reykjavik beer garden, working late into the night. Spools of vermillion thread cling to the space’s tarp roof; one member laboriously unwraps tinfoil and plasters it across plastic windows and walls; a ritual doll is suspended from the ceiling.   This haunting decor is being assembled for Falconfest, a noise show held in Reykjavik venue Lemmy in collaboration with No Borders, a charity dedicated to providing mutual aid to refugees. Spider Network, who organised the gig, have homed in on harsh noise as a way to fight the closures of spaces... The post Compilation of the Week: Plata’s Safn appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 冰岛噪音合辑《Safn》由厂牌Plata发行，收录多位年轻电子音乐人与实验创作者的作品。文章以Reykjavik啤酒花园中Spider Network乐队的演出场景切入，描绘他们用锡箔、丝线与仪式玩偶布置的表演空间，并联合难民互助组织No Borders举办Falconfest噪音演出，以此对抗雷克雅未克演出空间的关闭与士绅化进程。合辑整体聚焦硬核噪音与极端实验声响，作品既呈现冰岛地下场景的自治精神，也将噪音作为抵抗地产挤压与未来闭锁的政治工具。冰岛独立厂牌的出身赋予其鲜明的地域边缘色彩，但因正文仅为引言片段，专辑具体音乐细节与曲目分析较为有限。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Well John, it was my pleasure, though my answer dates four years after your thanks. Glad you enjoythis very special project.TBH, I delayed this review, because I didn't really know what to make of this album (lasting adouble LP release plus a 45RPM single) at acquisition time. Sure, the title announces that it willbe quite a program: Vertigo of Flaws: Emancipation of the Dissonance and Temperaments in IrrationalWaveforms and it doesn't lie about the sonic contents. The Diaz brothers have widened theirsoundscapes and we find some Industrial music (very early Popol Vuh and Kluster albums aren't far) to Ozric (well almost ;-))), but it's the former trend that dominates. In some ways, it feels a bitlike scrapping the bottom of the archives drawer (not sure it is the case, though), because the duoand their guest don't try to link the different bits, and there are odd stops inside the tracks'duration.As far as the Indus side, there is nothing aurally offensive (ala Throbbing Gristle), but nothingall that pleasant either and they're grouped in two packages, separated by the usual Trees Speaksoundscapes tracks. You'll still find great spoons of spices like Tangerine Dream, Cluster, early-Kraftwerk and the hypnotic "motorik" rock of Neu! or Can in the Emancipation of the Dissonance andTemperaments in Irrational Waveforms soup. Ultimately, despite a greater sonic scope, Vertigo ofFlaws is indeed flawed and overlong, and even overstays its welcome, partly because TS fail to renewitself, despite the greater spectrum presented here. Definitely not their best effort.
items._cn_summary: TREES SPEAK的《Vertigo of Flaws》以双张黑胶加单曲的篇幅呈现，融合早期Krautrock（Popol Vuh、Kluster、Cluster、Kraftwerk、Tangerine Dream）的氛围脉络与Neu!、Can式的motorik节奏，同时引入工业元素进行扩展。乐评指出专辑音景更为宽广，但段落之间缺乏有机衔接，曲目内部存在不自然的停顿，整体更像是从素材库中拼贴不同片段而非构建统一的聆听体验。尽管声谱范围扩大，但乐队未能真正更新自身的声音语言，长度过长导致听感冗余。作品在工业侧并不具备挑衅性，也未带来特别的愉悦感，更接近氛围与拼贴之间的实验折中，对偏好极端实验或纯粹工业的听众而言张力不足。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — During that busy yet fruitful year of 2017, following Flying Microtonal Banana and Murder of the Universe, came Sketches of Brunswick East; its title references the Melbourne suburb of Brunswick East and Miles Davis's 1960 LP Sketches of Spain. It is also a collaboration with the American group Mild High Club.It can also feel like a sequel to Paper M�ch� Dream Balloon, featuring bossa nova and an acoustic feel, yet it sets itself apart by seeming drenched in LSD, with a soft layer of psychedelia; the electric piano, drum grooves, and wah-wah guitar create a postmodern jazz-rock effect where the 60s meet the 90s and 2000s, and yet, in songs like "D-Day," it is microtonal.This album features some very interesting variations; the band experiments with pop, ranging from the array of percussion instruments to the use of vocals, backing harmonies, and the melodies themselves, sometimes with instruments following the vocals, and at other times doing the exact opposite, as seen in "Tezeta." The flute and Mellotrons create a distinctive atmosphere; combined with the 60s-style jazz they execute so well and those catchy choruses, they help shape the bohemian vibe sought in "The Spider and Me.""Sketches of Brunswick East II" introduces a recurring motif, tinged with the flamenco-esque flair that inspired it, that weaves through the entire album in various forms. When King Gizzard proposes a journey into the future, you have to buckle up; this time, however, they head into the past, embodying the roles like true method actors and channeling the musical sensibilities of that era. There is a space-age atmosphere, combined with a certain sophistication, that they capture brilliantly on "Dusk to Dawn on Lygon St." Meanwhile, "The Book" stands as another microtonal experiment; given that it was 2017, such a track was bound to make an appearance, yet it fits seamlessly with the album's playful psychedelia."A Journey to (S)Hell" offers a dose of urban chaos; just as Paper M�ch� Dream Balloon was the countryside, Sketches of Brunswick East is the city. A nocturnal journey awash in psychedelic lights unfolds suddenly, reconnecting with 70s-style synthesizers on "Rolling Stoned" before shifting to bossa nova on "You Can Be Your Silhouette." It is nearly impossible not to dance to this endless string of short songs, a fitting format, like small slides or snapshots of the city and open windows, each distinct in its own specific character."Sketches of Brunswick East III" brings the album to a close, and this peaceful interlude paves the way for the next chapter of 2017, Polygondwanaland, though that belongs to another dimension, one of the many inhabited by this Australian band.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / jazz-rock / bossa nova / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是澳洲乐队与Mild High Club的合作作品，标题致敬Miles Davis的《Sketches of Spain》，整体氛围向60年代爵士与迷幻音乐回归。电钢琴、哇音吉他与鼓组构成后现代爵士摇滚基底，融合bossa nova的舒缓节奏与微音律实验。配器上使用长笛、Mellotron与多种打击乐器，短曲形式如城市快照般串联，营造出波西米亚式的夜间漫游感。专辑中段以70年代合成器段落打破氛围，再回归bossa nova，体现出在实验框架内对流行旋律的探索。评论信息较为完整，厂牌为独立发行。整体虽有实验元素与跨风格融合，但更偏向复古迷幻爵士摇滚的复刻，对偏好激进前卫与电子实验的听众而言创新幅度有限。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Rounded up to the third star.Difficult to give it more, as Strange Terrain, because it is out of topic for this site, though you will find a bit of the madness that made Mice & Rats In The Loft so excellent, but musically this is nothing alike the first two albums. Here we're dealing with some New Wave - the 80's type - but way avant-la-lettre. So much so, that one can wonder whether these two unreleased sessions (not until 2010) were indeed recorded in 77. If that had been the case, it would be considered as groundbreaking had they been released back them. I some ways, some of the early tracks on this album are fun and can even qualify as Zolo-type of rock, and 80's Sparks aren't that far either. One can think of also later (as in recent) Aksak albums with Veronique Vincent. In the meantime, one can wonder why this archives compilation was released under the JDDG moniker, since the second salvo (bonus tracks) were labeled as Noy's Band. But in either case, if you're looking for JDDG soundscapes, you're not going to find much similar, though as I said the looniness is worth a listen.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Jan Dukes De Grey于1977年录制的未发行素材，直到2010年才以合辑形式面世。乐评指出其风格与乐队前两张作品截然不同，更接近新浪潮的早期雏形，具有明显的超前意识。曲目中呈现出Zolo式摇滚的趣味和80年代Sparks式的机巧感，同时也让人联想到Aksak与Veronique Vincent的合作质感。评论者认为某些早期段落甚至可视为具有开创性，但整体而言缺乏乐队标志性的声景氛围。附加曲目则以Noy's Band的名义收录，进一步模糊了作品归属。虽与乐队既有风格相去较远，但其怪诞气质仍值得一听。

items.body: “The Gray” is the second album by Italian producer Stefano Santi. Four years after his debut album, “JXDY”, the artist draws inspiration from themes such as love, loss, and collapse. He has also enlisted guest vocalists including Meldamor, Castelli, Contre Soirée, and Filmmaker. “The Gray” features a diverse range of influences—sometimes further accentuated by the guest vocalists—yet the album maintains a strong sense of cohesion. The opening track is brilliant, sounding like Shoegaze with subtle Dark-Wave undertones. These two influences remain prominent and, to my ears, constitute the album’s most compelling elements. However, you will also discover touches of Dream-Pop and even a more Dance-oriented track featuring Meldamor. The vocals are produced in a distinctive way, hovering in the background like a mist settling over the songs while still making their mark. Musically, I find the guitar work superb, particularly on the tracks leaning towards Shoegaze. Synth arrangements are also incorporated, at times heightening the atmosphere while adding a fresh dimension to the overall sound. The final track is an instrumental that feels like an outro, but one of exceptional quality. It stands out as a highlight in terms of atmosphere and provides a powerful conclusion to an album filled with gems. “The Gray” is a fantastic record that sounds like a distinctive fusion of several closely related genres. Definitely worth checking out! (Rating:8½). Listen to “Hxlding Time”: Hxlding Time by Never About Never Never is the solo project of Italian producer Stefano Santi, based in Milan. The project debuted with the album “JXDY” on 18 March 2022 (catalog VEYL033) on the Veyl label, recorded as instinct-led material that was not originally planned as a full-length. Santi’s first outside collaboration was a remix of Years Of Denial‘s “City Lights”, a step that carried into his second album, “The Gray”, released via Veyl on 26 June 2026 (catalog VEYL048) and built around guest contributions including Arizona duo Meldamor.
items._cn_summary: 意大利制作人Stefano Santi以Never名义发行的第二张专辑，融合了Shoegaze的吉他音墙与Dark-Wave的暗色氛围，辅以Dream-Pop质感与少量舞曲律动。客座人声如薄雾般悬浮于器乐层之上，既不抢夺空间又留下印记，形成统一的听觉气质。合成器编排为整体音色增添新鲜维度，吉他段落尤其出色，器乐尾声曲目以氛围取胜。专辑维持了紧凑的整体感，在多元素并置中未丧失方向性。Veyl厂牌的发行渠道赋予其地下独立属性，适合暗潮与另类电子交叉领域的听众。

items.album: 【ARBAN WEEKLY／今週の話題まとめ】ソニー・ロリンズとコルトレーン、唯一の共演盤に耳を澄ます
items.excerpt: 今週は、二人の巨人が一度きり交わした共演盤の再発から、101歳のサックス奏者が今なお更新し続ける現在進行形の音楽まで、時間の幅そのものがテーマになるようなニュースが並んだ。ジャズという文化が抱える「継続」の意味を、それぞれの記事から読み解きたい。 1956年、一度きりの夜—ロリンズとコルトレーンの共演盤が甦る Jazz Journal UKの新譜コラムに、ソニー・ロリンズとジョン・コルトレーンの唯一の共演を収めた録音『Tenor Madness』（1956年）のリイシュー情報が上がっている。二人は1956年、まだそれぞれが自身のスタイルを確立しきる前の時期に一度だけ同じセッションに立ち会った。これが二人の唯一知られている共演録音である。 この一枚が特別なのは、単に「二大テナーの共演」という肩書きのためではない。ロリンズとコルトレーンはその後、それぞれ全く異なる道をたどったことがジャズ史ではよく知られている。一般に、ロリンズはテーマを掘り下げる即興、コルトレーンはモード・ジャズを経てスピリチュアル・ジャズへと向かったとされる。まだ分岐する前の一夜の記録として、聴き直す価値がある一枚だと言
items.body: 今週は、二人の巨人が一度きり交わした共演盤の再発から、101歳のサックス奏者が今なお更新し続ける現在進行形の音楽まで、時間の幅そのものがテーマになるようなニュースが並んだ。ジャズという文化が抱える「継続」の意味を、それぞれの記事から読み解きたい。 1956年、一度きりの夜—ロリンズとコルトレーンの共演盤が甦る Jazz Journal UKの新譜コラムに、ソニー・ロリンズとジョン・コルトレーンの唯一の共演を収めた録音『Tenor Madness』（1956年）のリイシュー情報が上がっている。二人は1956年、まだそれぞれが自身のスタイルを確立しきる前の時期に一度だけ同じセッションに立ち会った。これが二人の唯一知られている共演録音である。 この一枚が特別なのは、単に「二大テナーの共演」という肩書きのためではない。ロリンズとコルトレーンはその後、それぞれ全く異なる道をたどったことがジャズ史ではよく知られている。一般に、ロリンズはテーマを掘り下げる即興、コルトレーンはモード・ジャズを経てスピリチュアル・ジャズへと向かったとされる。まだ分岐する前の一夜の記録として、聴き直す価値がある一枚だと言える。 同コラムでは他にも、スピリチュアルジャズ系五重奏やヘンリー・パーセル解釈作、サティをめぐるトランスアトランティック・トリオ、ユセフ・ラティーフへのトリビュート盤が紹介されている。まずはこのロリンズ×コルトレーン盤を軸に、ジャズ史の “ある分岐点” を聴き直す機会として楽しみたい。 出典：https://jazzjournal.co.uk/2026/09/13/new-releases-august-september-2026-r-s 101歳、いまも更新される音——マーシャル・アレンの新作 UK Jazz Newsが、101歳のサックス奏者マーシャル・アレンによる新作『101 – an Audio Odyssey』をレビューしている。アレンはサン・ラ・アルケストラの長年のメンバーとして半世紀以上を過ごしてきた人物で、サン・ラの没後はアレンがバンドを率いる立場になった。 サン・ラが説いた「宇宙」という主題は、しばしば神秘主義や奇矯なパフォーマンスの側面ばかりが語られがちだが、その根にあったのは既存の音楽語法・楽器編成・演奏形態そのものを問い直す姿勢だった。 アレンが101歳になった今もアルバムを作り続けているという事実は、その姿勢が個人の意志を超えて、ひとつの音楽的伝統として続いていることを示している。ジャズ史の生き証人がまだ現役で鳴らしている、という一点だけでも記録に値するニュースである。 出典：https://ukjazznews.com/marshall-allen-101-an-audio-odyssey グレッチェン・パーラト新作をガーディアン紙が賞賛 ジャズシンガーのグレッチェン・パーラトによる最新作『The Wise Ones』を、ガーディアン紙の評者ジョン・フォーダムが今月のジャズ・アルバムとして取り上げた。 本作では、フォークロックやジャズの影響を受けたマルチインストゥルメンタリストのアラン・ハンプトンや、パーカッショニストである夫のマーク・ジュリアナといった長年のパートナーに加え、ロバート・グラスパー、ミシェル・ンデゲオチェロ、ベッカ・スティーブンスといったゲストミュージシャンが参加している。 出典：https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/sep/11/gretchen-parlato-the-wise-ones-review チャールス・ロイド、インドとの対話を続ける理由 ジャズの長老チャールス・ロイドが、インド古典音楽の伝統との交錯を試みるプロジェクト「Sangam」の新作『Sangam & Friends』を発表した。Sangamは2004年から継続的に取り組まれてきたロイドのライフワークのひとつであり、今作でも複数の文化的背景を持つミュージシャンとの共演が展開されている。 ロイドはこれまでも、ジャズという語法の外側にある音楽的伝統との対話を繰り返し試みてきた奏者である。老境に差し掛かってなお、その探究を止めない姿勢は、ジャズという音楽が本来持っていた「異なるものを取り込みながら形を変え続ける」性質を体現しているとも言える。 出典：https://www.jazzthing.de/review/charles-lloyd-sangam-and-friends 投稿 【ARBAN WEEKLY／今週の話題まとめ】ソニー・ロリンズとコルトレーン、唯一の共演盤に耳を澄ます は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。
items._genre: jazz / free jazz / spiritual jazz / world fusion / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 本周乐评围绕几张爵士新发行展开。索尼·罗林兹与约翰·科尔蒂恩1956年唯一一次合作录音《Tenor Madness》再版，被视为两大 tenor sax 风格尚未分流前的关键节点；101岁的 Marshall Allen 推出新专辑《101 – an Audio Odyssey》，延续 Sun Ra 阿尔科斯特拉对乐器编制与演奏形态的颠覆传统；Charles Lloyd 的 Sangam 项目新作延续其与印度古典音乐传统的跨文化对话；Gretchen Parlato 的《The Wise Ones》获得《卫报》好评，集合 Robert Glasper、Michel Ndgeocello 等客座乐手。文章本身为新闻汇总性质，缺乏深入乐评与声音分析，但涵盖话题涉及 free jazz、spiritual jazz 与世界音乐融合，与学院派爵士及跨界融合口味有较高匹配度。
