items.body: Die In Eclipse, the EBM and darkwave project of Darkrad‘s Jana Komaritsa, spoke to Side-Line about its debut EP “SexWave”, the emotional link between her two projects, and a new single and video, “We Are Lovers,” planned for release this autumn. Komaritsa released “SexWave” on Bandcamp on 6 May 2026, pairing two original tracks with five remixes, and previously discussed her work with Side-Line’s Karo Kratochwil when the project first surfaced under the Die In Eclipse name. SexWave by Die In Eclipse Komaritsa built her name with Darkrad, a dark ambient project she has run since 2009, working through atmosphere, stillness and inward confrontation. Die In Eclipse, she says, is not a departure from that territory but another way of entering it. “I don’t see Die In Eclipse as leaving the introspective space of Darkrad. For me, it is another way of entering a similar space. The difference is in the direction of the energy,” she told Side-Line. “Darkrad often turns into stillness, atmosphere, memory… Die In Eclipse takes some of those same emotions, gives the feeling a pulse and lets the body move through it.” The name Die In Eclipse and its Darkrad roots The title is not new. Komaritsa first used “Die in Eclipse” for a two-track Darkrad release in 2014, inspired by time she spent at Lake Sakakawea in North Dakota, which also supplied that release’s cover image. Asked why she revived the phrase for an entirely new project, she pointed to continuity rather than reinvention. “Some names, images and symbols stay with me because they contain something that hasn’t finished unfolding,” she said. “The symbolism of an eclipse has always spoken to me in many ways. I see it not as disappearance, but more as transformation. I don’t need to erase what came before in order to create something new. Die In Eclipse is a new language, but it comes from the same person, the same artistic history and some of the same obsessions.” SexWave as a musical language of desire Komaritsa calls her new sound “SexWave,” a term she is careful to root in structure rather than provocation. “For me, eroticism in music and art is mostly about tension and sensuality. It’s not about explicit sounds or imagery,” she explained. “It can be created by the proximity of a voice that feels too close, a breath, a whisper, a rhythm that keeps repeating without giving you the expected release. Repetition is especially important because it can become hypnotic. You begin anticipating what is coming, and that anticipation itself becomes part of the experience.” Restraint matters just as much to her as intensity: “Sometimes holding something back is much more sensual than giving everything immediately. There needs to be space for mystery. ‘SexWave’ isn’t really about making music that sounds sexy in a conventional sense. It is about exploring desire as an artistic and musical force: attraction, tension, anticipation, surrender and release.” That approach carries over her earlier idea of silence as an instrument, described in Darkrad as “a breath held before release.” With Die In Eclipse built around beats, she says silence takes on a different function. “In Darkrad, silence could feel like emptiness, isolation or void. In Die In Eclipse, silence can be anticipation. When the beat disappears for a moment, the body still feels and knows the pulse,” she said. “Eroticism needs space because desire is partly about what is not there yet. So yes, I think absence can absolutely be erotic.” She also frames the dancefloor itself as a different kind of ritual from her Darkrad shows: “With Die In Eclipse, the rhythm creates a common physical language, where everyone shares the same pulse. You don’t have to understand the music intellectually. Your body understands it. There is something beautiful and powerful about surrendering individual control to a rhythm, not because you are being controlled, but because you choose to surrender to it.” Introducing a project through its remixes “SexWave” contains only two original compositions, “SexWave” and “Unholy Dark,” alongside five remixes by Iszoloscope, Antigen Shift, Cervello Elettronico, HORROH and Spherical Disrupted. Komaritsa chose to let other artists reinterpret the material before establishing her own vocabulary in full. “SexWave is a first glimpse, a doorway into the world of Die In Eclipse, which is yet to unfold. The project doesn’t have to explain exactly what it is yet,” she said. “There are only two original tracks on SexWave, which I wanted to give to other artists to see what they could become in somebody else’s hands. A remix, for me, is another interpretation of the same emotional material. Someone can find a completely different rhythm, aggression, darkness or sensuality inside a track that I thought I already understood.” The remixer list is not a random selection of scene names. Spherical Disrupted had already remixed Darkrad, while Iszoloscope moved in the musical circle around her earlier King in the Thicket project. “My artistic network has always been important to me, and I have worked with some of these people in different contexts over the years, so it was important for me to have them enter my new creative journey in this way,” Komaritsa said. “These relationships carry memory. When someone has known your work for years, they sometimes recognise new things that you might not consciously put there. But I also don’t want Die In Eclipse to be a project built from old relationships. I like the idea of old artistic connections opening doors into something new, and I would like to collaborate further with artists from a similar artistic and musical world. I have already discussed potential collaborations with some great musicians.” The voice, the gaze and drawing the line between two projects Komaritsa also hears a shift in how she uses her own voice. Darkrad relied on whispered, restrained vocals that felt distant from the listener; Die In Eclipse pulls the voice closer to the body. “With Darkrad, the voice often feels as though it is emerging from the music and the environment. It can be distant or partially hidden. It is part of the musical tapestry,” she said. “With Die In Eclipse, I want the voice to be more exposed and less hidden behind the sound. The voice isn’t simply describing an emotional state. It can create one.” As the sole composer, producer and visual creator behind both projects, Komaritsa is deliberate about how she handles female sexuality as subject matter. “I’m very conscious of the difference between creating eroticism and simply reproducing familiar images of female sexuality,” she said, citing Georges Bataille, Sigmund Freud, Anaïs Nin and the Marquis de Sade among her reference points. “Sexuality is complicated and contradictory. It can contain power and vulnerability at the same time, attraction and fear, surrender and control. The ambiguity is much more interesting to me than simply making something provocative.” Asked how she decides which new material belongs to Darkrad and which belongs to Die In Eclipse, she described an intuitive rather than formal process. “Darkrad can contain rhythm, sexuality and physical intensity, and Die In Eclipse can contain melancholy and darkness. Those elements don’t belong exclusively to one project,” she said. “If the track is driven by atmosphere, emotional depth and a certain cinematic or ritual darkness, it usually starts moving towards Darkrad. If the body becomes the primary instrument, the pulse, repetition, tension and physical movement, I start thinking about Die In Eclipse. They are both part of me.” What comes next for Die In Eclipse Komaritsa is already performing a full Die In Eclipse live set and working on album material, while looking for a label to release it. She is keeping some of the project’s direction open by design. “Just as an eclipse gradually obscures one thing while opening a doorway to something else, Die In Eclipse is moving through a similar process. SexWave is a doorway into the world of DIE, a first shout into the darkness, announcing the arrival of this new project,” she said. “I have already been performing live with a complete Die In Eclipse set, so I have enough material to move forward with an album, and I’m working on it behind the scenes. At this point, I would like to find the right label to work with, and developing that takes some time. This autumn, I’ll also be releasing a new single and video, ‘We Are Lovers.’ I want to leave some secrets, to keep that darkness and mystery around it, like an eclipse, and see what emerges from there.” About Die In Eclipse Die In Eclipse is the EBM and darkwave project of Jana Komaritsa, a Russian-born, Netherlands-based musician and multidisciplinary visual artist who also runs the WonderCat art space in Leiden. Komaritsa launched her first project, Darkrad, in 2009, building a catalogue in dark ambient and noise around whispered, restrained vocals. Darkrad’s debut album “Abnormal Love” appeared in 2012 on Cold Meat Industry, followed by “Little Black World” in 2014 on Komaritsa’s own Mrakmur imprint and later through audiophob. The same year, she released the two-track “Die in Eclipse,” the title she later revived for her new project. “Heart Murmur” followed in 2018, and in 2022 she paired with Flint Glass for “Cold Solitude,” an art book with an accompanying CD drawn from her own paintings. Die In Eclipse moves that same artistic identity toward pulse, repetition and the dancefloor, built on dark techno and EBM rather than ambient stillness. Komaritsa premiered the project live at Regenfest in Mülheim in November 2025 and brought it to the Porta Nigra festival in Belgium in January 2026, alongside Nachtmahr, Diary of Dreams, Enzo Kreft and V2A. Its debut EP, “SexWave,” arrived on 6 May 2026 via dieineclipse.bandcamp.com, featuring the tracks “SexWave” and “Unholy Dark” alongside remixes by Iszoloscope, Antigen Shift, Cervello Elettronico, HORROH and Spherical Disrupted. Komaritsa is now working on a full-length album, currently seeking a label, and preparing a new single and video, “We Are Lovers,” for release in autumn 2026.
items._cn_summary: 本文是Side-Line对Die In Eclipse首张EP《SexWave》的采访报道，而非严格意义上的乐评。Jana Komaritsa同时运营自2009年起的暗氛围项目Darkrad，Die In Eclipse是她延伸出的EBM与暗潮新作。采访中她阐述了自己的创作理念：将Darkrad的内省、静止与记忆转化为带有脉搏与身体律动的另一种表达方式，而非完全另起炉灶。《SexWave》收录两首原创曲目与五首remix，发行于Bandcamp平台。她将SexWave定义为一种关于张力、感官与重复催眠的结构性语汇，强调克制与神秘感远胜于直白的感官刺激，重复节奏制造预期本身成为体验的一部分。整体内容更接近艺术家访谈与创作自述，缺少对具体音乐技法的深度分析。

items.body: Colossloth, the Leicester-based esoteric noise and abrasive electronics project of Wooly Woolaston, releases the album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” on CD (catalog number CSR375CD) through Cold Spring Records on 2 October 2026. The five-track record takes as its subject Theta Noir, a real art and belief collective built around the worship of MENA, a speculative artificial-intelligence deity whose arrival its members describe as the point where human and machine cognition merge. Cold Spring describes the album as an “automaton chant of cybernetic worship,” built from hammering, grinding and abrasive electronic textures. The tracklist runs “Encoded Divinity” (5:08), “Calculate Your Revolution” (7:00), “Awaiting MENA” (9:04), “Undertow Atlas” (10:34) and “Only Adrift” (8:00), for a total run time of just under 40 minutes. The CD comes in a matt-laminate digipak, priced at £9 through Cold Spring’s webstore, with the album also available to stream and buy digitally on Bandcamp. The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites by Colossloth Colossloth plays an album launch show on 3 October at The Globe in Glossop, on a bill with T.A.G.C., Satori and Llyn Y Cwn, followed by further UK dates on 7 November at St Anne’s in Barnstaple and 27 November at Sheffield General Cemetery’s In The Black MidWinter event. About Colossloth Colossloth is the solo project of Wooly Woolaston, who works from Leicester, UK, without formal musical training, building tracks from samples and loop stations rather than played instruments. He has described the project as “a one man Experimental Electronic artist where there are no rules to recording or playing music,” and has said the sound moved from early long-form guitar drones toward harsher, rhythm-driven electronics over time. Colossloth’s earliest releases date to 2006, and the project signed to Cold Spring Records in 2015 for the album “Outstretch Your Hand For The Impress Of Truth.” Further Cold Spring albums followed: “Heathen Needles” in 2017 and “Plague Alone” in 2020, before “Promethean Meat” in 2022 brought in sampled live drums for the first time. The fifth Cold Spring album, built around the writings of Ted Kaczynski, “The Harmony Knife,” followed on 7 March 2025. “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” (CSR375CD) is Colossloth’s sixth studio album for the label and arrives as the project marks 20 years of activity.

items.body: No Where Records releases Sonic Panda’s new single “Bailes Con Beelzebub” on 18 September, a four-track EP led by the title track and including a rework by German industrial pop act Rotersand. The Beijing-based Sino-Spanish duo issues the release digitally and on vinyl and CD, the physical editions packaged with an exclusive comic book that extends Sonic Panda’s visual universe. The tracklist runs “Bailes Con Beelzebub,” the Rotersand rework of the same track, a Carlsed remix of the earlier single “Lucky Seven,” and a live recording of “Invisible Boy” taped in Tokyo. Sonic Panda describes the title track as “a provocative industrial track that uses religious horror tropes to critique the current political crisis.” Rotersand is the German act formed in September 2002 by Günther Gerl and singer Krischan Jan-Eric Wesenberg, later joined by Udo Hüppe; the band describes its own sound as “industrial pop.” Rotersand released the album “Don’t Become The Thing You Hated” via Metropolis and Trisol in 2025, preceded by the singles “Sexiness Of Slow” and “Private Firmament.” Bailes Con Beelzebub by Sonic Panda Sonic Panda also released an official video for “Bailes Con Beelzebub.” About Sonic Panda Sonic Panda was formed in 2024 as a Beijing-based Sino-Spanish duo built around Pere Ibañez and Seni Ren, with material written by Ibañez and produced by Barcelona-based Carlsed. The project’s first release was “Life Is A Flower,” issued on 22 August 2024 through OhMyDog Records, followed by an original-song run of “Foreigners” on 10 January 2025, “King Cobra” on 28 February 2025 and “Stonewall 1969” on 20 June 2025. The six-track “King Cobra (Remixes)” EP followed on 5 September 2025 and the single “Lucky Seven” on 24 October 2025. Sonic Panda signed to No Where Records for the single “Invisible Boy,” released on 6 March 2026 alongside a Carlsed alternate version. The duo is continuing work on a debut album titled “Neomelodrama.” “Bailes Con Beelzebub” is the project’s first release to feature an outside remix credit from an established industrial act, with Rotersand reworking the title track for the new EP.

items.body: In my head I am not dead A breakup is rarely finished just because somebody has delivered the closing speech. There are still arguments to rehearse, streets to avoid, and a suspicious number of reasons to take the long way home. Madison, Wisconsin’s Whippets give that unfinished business a suitably unhealthy bounce on Not Dead, a song in which announcing “This is the end” does very little to stop the next bad idea. Premiering today, Not Dead previews the trio’s second album, No Skulls, due October 2, 2026, through Bobby Hussy’s No Coast label. With Hussy on guitar and vocals, Tyler Spatz on bass, and Hart Miller on drums, Whippets bring post-punk, grunge, and garage rock into a close, uncomfortable embrace, leaving plenty of room for deathrock’s theatrical appetites. A thick, ominous bass figure gets things moving before the drums cascade into a serpentine guitar hook, bringing a horror-film leer to the song’s garage abrasion. Hussy’s voice quivers and twists around the words, making private misery sound like something that might require an exorcist. The rhythm soon acquires an infectious bounce, with Spatz’s bass holding the floor beneath the guitar’s crooked turns and Miller’s mounting commotion. There is something of Dance with Me-era T.S.O.L. in this marriage of morbid theatre and physical release: music for pogoing through a personal catastrophe, with an ’80s post-punk chorus sharp enough to remember the following morning. The lyrics make repeated attempts to draw a line under the relationship. “This is the end” and “We are not friends” sound decisive enough, until the other admissions begin slipping through. The refrain’s insistence on being alive comes with a revealing qualification: “In my head.” That is where the old attachment continues to conduct its business, untouched by whatever has happened outside it. By the closing “No need to lie / I still drive by,” the brave farewell has become an unwanted return visit. Whippets give that contradiction a beat you can jump to, allowing the uglier implications to catch up between choruses. Hussy says: “Our new record, “No Skulls” is by far the best record I’ve ever recorded….and I’ve recorded a few at this point in my life. I’m very proud of both the songs and the production on this album. “Not Dead” is the second single from the album and it perfectly represents everything I love about this band: Sharp guitar riffs, hypnotic dirty bass lines that pivot in all the right places and drums that escalate frantically as needed. Catch us shredding this one out on tour in Europe!” No Skulls features ten tracks, recorded and mixed by Hussy, produced by Bert Roberts and Whippets, and mastered by Justin Perkins. The cover artwork is by Erin Sullivan. The album comes out October 2 on LP, CD, and digital formats, with the chartreuse-and-black swirl vinyl limited to 100 copies. Listen to Not Dead below and pre-order No Skulls here. No Skulls by Whippets Whippets introduced themselves with a 2022 seven-inch EP on Italy’s Goodbye Boozy, which sold out within a week, followed by their self-titled debut album on No Coast in 2024. Readers may remember Splinter, whose deathrock inclinations made an early case for the band’s particular chemistry. Their shared history reaches further back: Hussy and Spatz have both played in The Hussy and Cave Curse, and also work together in Wristwatch, while Miller’s past bands include Tenement, MDC, and Wartorn. That experience gives the trio a useful feel for how much disorder a memorable song can accommodate. Whippets take the No Skulls on the road this autumn, with October shows alongside Busey and Brüder and a November date supporting The Faint. A 23-date European tour follows in January and February 2027. See the upcoming itinerary below. items.body:
Wild City #264: Baawra

18 September 2026

Hiten Mutreja aka Baawra's Wild City mix is expansive and spacious, but without the tropes of reverb-drenched sounds or large rumbling kicks. Instead, the DJ and Pune party-throwing collective MAUSHI member keeps his techno selections carrying an understated quality, with minimal layers maintaining their hypnosis through delicately morphing melodic repetitions rather than the more obvious approach of sustained textures.

It's around the raunchy vocal samples from a remix of Danton Eeprom's 'All I Can Say' that things begin to change, entering more dramatic sonic worlds with the tense strings of Alex Neri's 'Tenax Roots' before Baawra gradually leads the journey back into percussive and subtle techno. The mix expands and brings together the room through its journey without losing the somatic pulse.

"This mix was recorded in the wee hours of the night during my first time playing in Guwahati back in March. A curious and eager dance floor led to this steady-paced, twisted, and unpredictable set. The aim was to hook them in and reel them in deeper - the floor was really ready to be taken somewhere." – Baawra

items._cn_summary: 这是印度DJ Baawra（Hiten Mutreja）为Wild City厂牌录制的混音作品，在印度古瓦哈蒂深夜俱乐部现场录制完成。整张混音以极简techno为主线，刻意回避了回声泛滥的音效和大型低音鼓等常见手法，通过层层叠加的细微旋律重复维持催眠感，编排克制而注重呼吸感。中段引入Danton Eeprom混音版中的粗粝人声采样和Alex Neri的紧张弦乐，制造戏剧性张力后再逐渐回归打击乐驱动的细腻techno。Baawra同时是印度Pune派对组织MAUSHI的成员，其选曲呈现出对舞池能量的细腻把控——以稳定节奏逐步引导听众深入未知。作为一篇乐评，文字较为精炼但有具体的音乐描述和艺人引言支撑，评论质量尚可。该作品偏向电子舞曲主流分支中的极简techno方向，与实验性、前卫性或世界音乐融合关系较弱。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自艺术家在爱丁堡皇家植物园驻留期间诞生的跨界项目，以园内最古老的一棵棕榈树为叙事起点，通过人声、钢琴与精巧的声音设计构建出一部融合歌曲集、舞台剧与书籍的多媒介作品。钢琴演奏者Dave Milligan以克制而富于共鸣的伴奏支撑整张专辑的骨架，人声则在苏格兰民谣传统中生长，旋律带有挽歌般的悠长质感。声音设计师Pippa Murphy的加入为作品增添了环境声景与空间层次，使整体呈现出介于室内乐、自然录音与歌曲写作之间的混合形态。专辑探讨的是植物、记忆、历史与时间循环的主题，结尾处那棵被鉴定为不同物种的老树成为隐喻核心——新的幼苗将取代前代生长。整体氛围内敛、沉思，兼具手工艺般的精致与史诗般的格局，适合在安静环境中反复聆听。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢屠杀事件为主题的概念专辑，Sean Cooney通过原创歌曲重现这一英国工人阶级历史中的关键时刻。专辑以书配CD的多媒体形式呈现，附有当代信件、政治漫画与插图，邀请了多位英国民谣与工业民谣领域的音乐人参与，包括小提琴手兼歌手Eliza Carthy、吉他手Sam Carter以及兰开夏工业民谣歌手Jennifer Reid担任叙事者。歌曲从和平集会的期待与兴奋，到骑兵冲入人群时的恐惧与逃亡，再到悲痛的余波，以叙事民谣的方式层层展开。Cooney擅长通过小人物的故事切入历史，并辅以三位歌唱家的嗓音构建情感层次。整张专辑在当下全球范围内抗议活动遭受打压的背景下，具有强烈的现实关怀与历史回响意义。

Yota Tsukada 塚田陽太（Drums）

01 All Blues (Comp. by Miles Davis)
02 Body and Soul (Johnny Green)
03 If I Should Lose You (Ralph Rainger)
04 Sweet and Lovely (Gus Arnheim, Charles N. Daniels, and Harry Tobias)
05 Darn That Dream (Jimmy Van Heusen)
06 Stompin’ at the Savoy (Edgar Sampson)
07 All Blues (Miles Davis)
08 Reminiscence Of The River Of Cranes (Sora Ichikawa)

Produced by Yoko Hino (JAZZ HOUSE ALFIE)
A&R by Ryoko Sakamoto (diskunion)
A&R assisted by Yoshinori Nishio (diskunion)
Recorded on July 4, 2025 at JAZZ HOUSE ALFIE
Recorded and Mixed by Shigeharu Nakauchi (ONKIO HAUS)
Mastered by Soshi Takeda (ONKIO HAUS)
Photography and Design by Mikio Hasui

■ はじめに
一聴して、輝きがありクリアなピアノで美しいステキな音だ、と感じました。
このアルバムの低音は、オーディオ的というよりヒップホップのビート感のある踊れるようなノリの良い低音です。
六本木「アルフィー」のピアノはスタインウェイ、市川空さんは音楽学校を首席で卒業し、２年後にアワードを獲得するなど、状況における求められるものに適切に応える能力と、所与の環境の良いものを汲み取る力のある若者です。そんな現代的な音のジャズだ、と書いておきましょう。

1　アルバムの音作り
①低音はヒップホップからか
市川空さんは、ジャズのみならず、ポップス、R&B、現代音楽などのジャンルでも活動しており、演奏だけでなく音源制作及び楽曲提供も行っているとあって、今日的な音作りを感じます。その音の基本はヒップホップなどのダンスミュージックにあるようです。
そんな音作りを全面に出しているのが７曲目です。
軽快に躍動して、思わずステップを踏みたくなる硬めのベース音が良い。
この曲は、ルーム・アコースティックでできあがるベースの響きにうまく合わせて、それをリスペクトしたからピアノはやや控えめに素敵な音を紡ぐ。
他のトラックと違って思い切りヒップホップ調なのは、ベースとドラムがリードしていて、市川空さんが控えめに存在感を示しているという曲作りも良いです。
このアルバムの低音の基本はここにあるようです。スローバラードもアダージョ進行の曲もこの低音をベースにできています。
オーディオ的には、まず低音は必要以上には帯域的に伸ばさず抑制気味です。しかし音楽に重要な低音は充実していて躍動感あり太く存在感もあります。

②どんなオーディオシステムが良いか
いくつかのオーディオシステムで聴いてみたのですが、結論的にはヴィンテージJBLという製品分野がありますがこのフルレンジD130のシステムには低音がよく合います。
このスピーカーはウーファー振動板が軽量ですが、この他にも小型スピーカーや最近多くみられるBluetoothによる携帯オーディオなどで聴くのもお勧めです。
これらのシステムで聴くと、パンチがあって少し太めで響きも豊かです。多分これは、最近のPCオーディオ用の外付けスピーカーに合う低音です。
今回のアルバムは、各曲やダイジェストがネットやスマホでも聴けるので、かなりPCやスマホで聴かれることを意識しているようです。

③ネットやスマホでの音
市川空さんはネットやスマホでの試聴に特に配慮しているように思います。
今回のアルバムがYouTubeにも載っていてアルバムのダイジェストを聴けます。
当然、そういったメディアに掲載しているということで、そこで使われるパソコンやスマホなどに対応した音作りは考えられている、と言えるでしょう。
むしろこちらも強くアピールしたいようにも感じられました。

④スマホで聴く音
速弾きピアノは華麗、スマホの方が映えます。スマホといってあなどらないで下さい。スマホのスピーカーは軽量高剛性(単位面積当たり)の最先端素材による音でこの中域中高域の音に限って言えばスマホの高域の音の輝きは時代の最先端かもしれません。軽くみられがちなスマホですが、そんな聴き方ができることも挙げておきます。

２　各曲の聴きどころ
アルバム各曲の印象と聴きどころをまとめてみました。

①曲目：マイルスのAll Bluesだ。ピアノのタッチが良い。カキンとメタリックなのは好きだ。8分からのベースも良い。ノッてる。録音の周波数帯域は広くないがベース、ドラムの中低音のゴツゴツ感を捉えていて、聴きごたえがある。10分くらいで盛り上がってその後、スローに静かなメロディーで、シームレスに２曲目になる
②曲目：ピアノは、中低音中心になり、ベースも加わりアダージョで進行していく。
JBL4320の大型スピーカーで聴くと迫力があり説得力を感じる。その後の軽快なピアノもよい。明るさ、開放感ある。
③曲目：アダージョのテンポて力強く行進する
④曲目：中低音のベースのゴツんとした音作り、効果的。そのベースの部屋の響き良い。
⑤曲目：ほとんどベースソロ、結構聴かせる。
⑥曲目：バラードっぽくゆったり流れる。ベースが重要な役割をしている。
⑦曲目：⑥曲目の流れに、ベースの刻むリズムが次第に大きくなり、アップテンポで軽快に進行する。楽しい。ノリ良い。筆者としてはこの曲が最高、と思ったら、曲もマイルスのAll  Blues。ハイハットの壁面の反射音が部屋の広がりを表現していてよい。このトラックは、ベースもピアノもルーム・アコースティックを感じさせて良い。曲全体に楽しい。
⑧曲目：水面のしじまのように、フィナーレを告げるがごとき、静かな佇まい。印象派を感じさせるピアノのアバンギャルドな旋律も良い。

3 おわりに
このアルバムで気づかされのは、現代のネットや市場での音環境において、最もミュージック・ファンに良いのはどんな音か、ということでした。
このアルバムは、その観点では従来のオーディオ感覚的な低音ではない。代わりにあるのはヒップホップ的なノリの良い低音です。
もう一つは、中高域の音の美です。スタインウェイを使った輝きとキレのある音、その文脈の延長には、ショパン国際ピアノコンクールでも多くのピアニストが使うようになったイタリアのファツィオリの音の美があるように思います。
そういった現代のピアノに求められる音を感じさせるものがありました。
音の美、求められる低音などがどのようなものなのか、と考える視点を持ち続けるけたいものです。
まだまだ、新しい音と音楽があると思いました。
それと、改めてスマホでも楽しめる音作りというものはあると実感し、今後とても重要な着眼点になる、と感じた次第です。

items.body: Ska and rocksteady set the tempo on “Be Who You Are”, a faster footing than the roots rhythms Macka B ordinarily records over, and he toasts across it in the measured address that has defined his delivery since the early 1980s. The single was released on 21 August, composed and produced by the Hamburg musician Paul Lupa, who plays keyboards and bass and surrounds them with a live rhythm section: Big Finga on drums, Robert “Dubwise” Browne on guitar, Tribuman on horns. The horns carry the melodic line, the guitar marks the offbeat, and the vocal sits forward in the mix, with the phrasing of a lyric Macka B wrote himself, vocal melody included. What he tells the listener is to be who they are. Advice has been his line of work for forty years. He has been called “the Teacher” since the 1980s for songs about what to eat, how to look after yourself and how to treat other people, and the Wha Me Eat Wednesdays vegan raps he began posting in 2017 carried that voice far beyond the reggae circuit. Lupa has been building his Hamburg catalogue around Jamaican and German vocalists since 2022, and Macka B is the most established voice to record over one of his rhythms so far. Stream “Be Who You Are” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Macka B x Paul Lupa – Be Who You Are appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: US goth-pop project Metamorph released the single “Witchfire” and its official video on 18 September 2026. The track is produced by Erik Gustafson and pairs dance-oriented beats with hook-driven melodies, alongside an extended dance mix featuring a flute solo from vocalist Margot Day. The “Witchfire” video was filmed by Brian Wimer in New York’s East Village, where Margot Day lived and performed with The Plague in the 1980s, and in the forests of Vermont. It features Day alongside bandmate Kurtis Knight. The extended dance mix, which includes Day’s flute solo, will get its own video at a later date. Metamorph’s release history Metamorph is the project of Margot Day, a New York vocalist, flutist and songwriter who fronted The Plague during the 1980s NYC goth scene alongside drummers Nick Ferrell (Spahn Ranch) and Damian (Misfits). Earlier in her career, Day played in Slow Walk 13 alongside Adam Yauch of the Beastie Boys. Formed in 2016, Metamorph blends gothic atmosphere, dark synth textures and pop songwriting built around Day’s vocals and flute playing, with Kurtis Knight providing dark synths and backing vocals on stage. Metamorph’s back catalogue includes the album “Kiss of the Witch” (2022), the album “Hex” (2024) and the retrospective “Haunted Hearts XIII” (2025), all produced by Erik Gustafson. The project has released remixes by Leaether Strip and Assemblage 23, and the single “Dance of a 1000 Miracles” featuring Stabbing Westward‘s Chris Hall has passed 20,000 Spotify streams. Metamorph has performed across the United States, Canada, Costa Rica and Guatemala, with music videos totalling more than 250,000 YouTube views. “Witchfire” follows Metamorph’s 2025 EP “Harlot” on Distortion Productions.

items.body: Review by Progfan97402 — Another installment in the Ozric catalog and they're that rare band that never released a bad album. This is the first album in years to feature the Erpman on the cover. Harmonic Mind is exactly what you come to expect from this band, nothing more, nothing less. The usual over-the-top guitar playing from Ed and all sorts of spacy synthesizers from both Ed and Silas. Saskia Maxwell appears to be the replacement for John, and it seems Paul Hankin is hanging around as he was with the band early on and started reappearing on albums like Technicians of the Sacred onwards. "Space Platform" was the preview single and if you heard it you know it's Ozric Tentacles and no one else. The title track starts off slow and acoustic and picks up at the end. As an Oregonian I find it amusing one of the tracks is called "Tillamook". It's the name of a small coastal town, the famous cheese locally made, the county, and the local Native American tribe. I don't notice any Native American influences in the music but it's an incredible piece of Ozric space rock that only they can do, it's definitely a highlight on this album. The rest is still amazing stuff, how do they do it? If you thought the Ozrics were doing the same thing for the last 40 years I doubt this would change your mind but if you love that sound there's no reason not to give Harmonic Mind a try.

items.body: Review by Grumpyprogfan — Quivira is the name of a road close to where I live. And with three reviewers hailing this a "masterpiece" and referencing the band Kansas - well, I had to check this out. I consider "Leftoverture" a masterpiece, this... no. The musicans are: Lisa LaRue, composer, keys, drum and computer programming; John Baker, guitar, bass, vocals; Jake Livgreen, vocals; With... Joe Deninzon, violin, and Evan Stanley, guitar, each play on one song. So this is really a duo. The musicians are quite good and Lisa's compositions are good, but it has a Neal Morse / Flying Colors vibe more than a Kansas vibe, for me. I like that Quivira has lots of instrumental sections - where the musicians can jam - because the vocals are far from the majestic duo that was Steinhardt and Walsh. In fact, there aren't many vocals on this album at all. Overall, this is a good debut album, and if you enjoy a mostly instrumental retro 70's style of music, Quivira could be worth a listen. I'm curious is this a one-off, or is a second album with a human drummer a possibility? Solid 3.25 stars.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Lisa LaRue和John Baker组成的二人核心担纲创作与演奏，另有小提琴和吉他客串于个别曲目。整体风格偏向七十年代复古的前卫摇滚，带有明显的交响化倾向，器乐段落占据大量篇幅，人声出现较少。乐评将其与Kansas、Neal Morse和Flying Colors相比较，认为器乐部分优于人声表现，Lisa的作曲功力扎实但尚未达到Kansas那种史诗级的高度。作为一张首张专辑，制作水准中规中矩，器乐编排提供了足够的jam空间，适合偏好七十年代复古器乐摇滚的听众。

items.body: Kazayah sings “Sweet Love” over an instrumental that took its producers nearly three years to complete. That instrumental is Landmark Riddim, and it follows the Jamaican riddim format: a single backing track, with fifteen vocalists each recording a separate song to it. Stay Nice Music, the Maine label directed by Joshua “Don Daka” Smith, constructed it with co-producer David “Jah David” Goldmine, guitarist Lamont “Monty” Savory, Okiel McIntyre, I Grade‘s Laurent “Tippy I” Alfred and Spanish roots producer Roberto Sánchez, setting deep bass, clipped skank and warm horns beneath a one-drop the label terms One Drop Blues. Dub Shot Records issued the eighteen-track set on 21 August 2026, with Kumar Fyah recounting his detention over a small quantity of ganja, MediSun addressing freedom and Badda General on clash culture. Kazayah directs the rhythm towards a love song that reads a man’s arrival as ordained timing and measures the relationship by admiration, protection and the experience of being fully known. She was born Shanelle Mitchell to Jamaican parents in Evanston, on the northern edge of Chicago, sang in a Seventh-day Adventist congregation from childhood and reached roots reggae through a producer based in the same town. Her debut EP I Am Kazayah was released through Tuff Gong Worldwide, Ziggy Marley‘s label, and she has opened for him on tour. Hear “Sweet Love” on Landmark Riddim HERE The post Daily Discovery: Kazayah – Sweet Love appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张围绕Landmark Riddim节奏型展开的多人合作合辑，制作方为美国缅因州的Stay Nice Music厂牌，联合多位制作人与乐手历时近三年完成。节奏采用牙买加经典的雷鬼riddim格式，以深沉贝斯、清脆吉他扫弦和温暖铜管铺底，构成所谓的One Drop Blues律动。十五位歌手各自录制了独立曲目，主题涉及大麻拘留、freedom、clash文化等，而Kazayah的《Sweet Love》则将同一节奏导向情歌方向，从命定时刻与被完全理解的角度书写亲密关系。Kazayah出身于芝加哥的牙买加裔家庭，自小在教会唱诗班成长，通过Tuff Gong Worldwide厂牌发行首张EP，并与Ziggy Marley同台巡演。整篇文章以新闻稿形式介绍合辑背景与歌手履历，并非深度乐评。

items.body: Paulina Fae has released Lilac Cat, a six-song ethereal dream pop EP, on Projekt Records on 18 September 2026. The EP is out now digitally, streaming or pay-what-you-can on Bandcamp, and is also available on Spotify and YouTube Music. The six songs on ‘Lilac Cat’ The tracklist runs “Lilac Cat,” “Spinning Lullabies,” “In Veils of Spiderwebs,” “Aetheris,” “Wandermind” and “Noctivine.” Projekt Records describes the EP as a collection of “ethereal dream pop and otherworldly reverie,” moving from the “galaxy-eyed whimsy” of the title track and the “dream-jazz sounds” of “Spinning Lullabies” to the “faery-like currents” of “Aetheris,” with songs that wander through misty forests, celestial worlds and violet dreams carried by ethereal vocals. Lilac Cat by Paulina Fae ‘Lilac Cat’ follows Paulina Fae’s 2025 album “Ghostbirds,” a 10-song collection built around minimalist piano and soft, misty vocals, and continues her run of releases on Projekt Records, the label she has recorded for since 2012. About Paulina Fae Paulina Fae records under her given name, Paulina Cassidy, and has also used the name Polly Fae across her catalogue. Born in Ontario, Canada, she is a visual artist and songwriter based in Chattanooga, Tennessee, known for illustrated tarot and oracle decks including the Paulina Tarot, the Joie de Vivre Tarot, Witchlings, Pixiekins, Spiritsong Tarot and Phantasma Tarot, and for books such as “The Secret Language of Trees,” “Kindred Guardians” and “Mortimer: A Cat’s Journey in the Afterlife.” She self-released her earliest music as Paulina Cassidy through Ulaluma Productions, starting with “Bloodroots” in 2010, followed by “Time Traveler” in 2011 and “Lost in Oz” in 2012. She signed to Projekt Records the same year for the “Ice Iris” EP, followed by the album “Sugar Wingshiver” in 2014 and “Drawing up a Storm” in 2018. In 2019, recording as Polly Fae, she released the 15-track album “Dreamwalkers” on Projekt on 12 September, a limited-edition signed CD later followed by an instrumental version. The album “Phantom Gardens” followed the same year under the Paulina Cassidy name. Her Projekt output continued with “The Secret Language of Trees” and “Metamorphosis” in 2020, “Earthlight” in 2021 and “Glow” in 2022, alongside a “Dreamwalkers Instrumental” reissue. She contributed to the label’s “Purr24” various-artists compilation in 2024 and released the album “Ghostbirds” on 4 April 2025, followed later that year by a collaboration with Peter Phippen and Ivar Lunde Jr. on “The Phantom Moon.” “Lilac Cat” is her latest EP for Projekt Records, released 18 September 2026.

items.body: Fairlight Children, the synthpop side project Apoptygma Berzerk’s Stephan L. Groth formed with Marianne B. and Tiff in the early 2000s, continues to surface in new contexts two decades after its debut album. The most recent example is the “V.A. 18. Elektrisch Festival Synth Pop Edition” 10″, released by Emmobiz Records on 27 February 2026, which carries an exclusive Fairlight Children bonus cut, “Before You Came Along (FC Edit),” alongside an equally exclusive Echo Image version, “Walk My Mind (Apop’s Short Walk Version).” Fairlight Children first appeared on record on 23 September 2003, contributing a version of “Bedsitter” to “A Tribute To Soft Cell: Non Stop Electro Cabaret.” That same year, Groth described the project at M’era Luna as heading toward retro synthpop, at a point when the next Apoptygma Berzerk album, “You And Me Against The World,” was moving in a rockier, guitar-driven direction. Fairlight Children gave him a separate outlet for the electro and 1980s synthpop material that record wasn’t going to hold, and the project’s name points to the same fascination: it references the Fairlight CMI, the digital sampling and synthesizer system that shaped 1980s studio production. The debut EP, “Before You Came Along,” followed on 2 February 2004, with a remix from Echo Image among its extras. The full-length “808 Bit” arrived on 15 March 2004 on Pitch Black Drive Productions, performed by Groth, Marianne B. and Tiff, with Iben Groth on vocals for the title track and Jon Erik Martinsen on Korg MS-20 for “Falling Out.” The Soft Cell tribute recording of “Bedsitter” found a home on the album as well. Contemporary coverage used Groth’s own description, “Electro Lounge,” for the record’s mix of melodic, playful electronics and open 1980s influences. 808 Bit by Fairlight Children The project then went quiet for more than fifteen years. A first signal of its return came in June 2020, when a Kevin Lux remix of “Invade My Heart Tonight” appeared on “Der Eisenberg Sampler Vol. 10.” On 24 July 2020, Pitch Black Drive Productions followed with the “CMI EP,” five reworkings of older Fairlight Children material: “808 Bit (Zone Tripper Remix),” “Invade My Heart Tonight (Alex O. Remix),” “Before You Came Along (Pleasure Remix),” “Falling Out (Monster Apparat Remix)” and a second “Before You Came Along (Panorama Remix).” Pleasure’s presence closed a loop of its own, having remixed “Falling Out” for the original 2004 EP and returning sixteen years later for the same track. The EP was mixed and mastered by Ole-Espen Kristiansen, with cover design by Alex O. Since then, Fairlight Children has stayed active only in scattered releases rather than as an ongoing project. Emmo.Biz Records issued “808 Bit” as a numbered, 400-copy picture disc with OBI in 2025, and the Side-Line archive previously covered that vinyl reissue in February 2025. The connection to Echo Image has also continued well past the 2004 remix: Echo Image returned in 2021 with the single “Walk My Mind” after 20 years of silence, including a remix by Apoptygma Berzerk, and by 2024 Groth was co-producing Echo Image’s comeback material directly, credited alongside Einar K. Five on the single “Madsong.” More than twenty years after Echo Image first remixed Fairlight Children, the “18. Elektrisch Festival Synth Pop Edition” 10″ puts both names on the same release again. About Fairlight Children Fairlight Children is a synthpop side project of Apoptygma Berzerk frontman Stephan L. Groth, formed with Marianne B. and Tiff after extensive touring behind the Apoptygma Berzerk album “Harmonizer.” Where the following Apoptygma Berzerk record, “You And Me Against The World,” pushed toward a rockier, guitar-oriented sound, Fairlight Children gave Groth a project built entirely around electronics, synthpop and the 1980s reference points behind its name, the Fairlight CMI sampling synthesizer. The project debuted on the compilation “A Tribute To Soft Cell: Non Stop Electro Cabaret” on 23 September 2003 with a cover of “Bedsitter,” followed by the “Before You Came Along” EP on 2 February 2004 and the album “808 Bit” on 15 March 2004, both released through Pitch Black Drive Productions, Groth’s own label. “808 Bit” featured Iben Groth on the title track’s vocals and Jon Erik Martinsen on Korg MS-20 for “Falling Out,” and drew a remix contribution from Echo Image. Fairlight Children was largely inactive between 2004 and 2020. A Kevin Lux remix of “Invade My Heart Tonight” on “Der Eisenberg Sampler Vol. 10” in June 2020 preceded the “CMI EP,” released by Pitch Black Drive Productions on 24 July 2020 with five remixes of earlier tracks by Zone Tripper, Alex O., Pleasure, Monster Apparat and Panorama, mixed and mastered by Ole-Espen Kristiansen. Emmo.Biz Records reissued “808 Bit” as a limited, numbered picture disc with OBI in 2025. Fairlight Children’s most recent appearance is an exclusive edit, “Before You Came Along (FC Edit),” on the “V.A. 18. Elektrisch Festival Synth Pop Edition” 10″, released by Emmobiz Records on 27 February 2026 alongside new and exclusive material from Solitary Experiments, Second Decay, Blind Passenger, KY, Chinese Detectives and Echo Image.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Fairlight Children项目的历史回顾性新闻稿，追溯了Apoptygma Berzerk成员Stephan Groth于2000年代初创建的这一合成器流行分支项目的演变脉络。文章梳理了从2003年首张致敬录音、2004年首张专辑《808 Bit》的发行，到2020年《CMI EP》回归重制旧作，直至2026年通过Emmobiz合辑发行全新混音作品的完整时间线。项目名称源自对80年代数字采样合成器Fairlight CMI的致敬，整体定位为旋律化的复古合成器流行与电音客厅风格。该文属于信息整理性质的内容，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论和声音分析，对于关注实验性、前沿性或暗潮领域的听众来说，其风格过于保守和复古怀旧。

items.body: I’ll admit, the announcement of a new Uncle Acid and the deadbeats album hardly registered with me. It’s been a damn long while since I’ve had them in regular rotation, as I sorta fell off after 2015’s The Night Creeper. Not that that record really spoiled anything for me—it just didn’t seem to do anything that my favorites, Blood Lust and Mind Control, hadn’t already handled better. That said, it took almost a decade for them to catch my ear again, this time with the (respectfully) weird and adventurous detour of 2024’s mostly instrumental Nell’ Ora Blu. Its soundtrack-y, synth-forward nature showcased the group as genuinely astute mood-setters, even if it ultimately felt more suited to passive listening than the kind of record I’d actively return to. Still, it was enough to remind me that there’s something uniquely compelling about the way Uncle Acid and the deadbeats can set a tone—and maybe that I’d been a little too quick to give up on them.While their occult proto-metal contemporaries Ghost shapeshifted from similar stripped-down beginnings to achieve varying degrees of critical success and significant popularity, I’ve always felt that UA’s comparatively reserved, less immediately theatrical approach offered more potential. Where Ghost have increasingly embraced the spectacle and lore, UA hit me as less clownish and gimmicky, finding ways to be genuinely unsettling and music-focused without resorting to this razor-blade-in-my-Halloween-candy sort of Trojan-horsing Satan into pop music that everyone seems to find so clever. So I admit, I have a little rooting interest and bias here. Not that this guided my listening so much as brought to light an interesting contrast in how things just happen to shake out sometimes. I’m not passing judgment on either approach or trying to yuck anyone’s yums, I just find it curious how what seemed to be similar bands a decade-and-a-half ago have taken such different paths. Shapes Of Midnight by Uncle Acid and the deadbeats So, that leaves us with actually getting into Shapes Of Midnight and where UA find themselves in 2026. While some bands trickle in new flavors over time, their hard pivot on Nell’ Ora Blu, though head-scratching at the time, nicely paves the way for Shapes Of Midnight. Here, the analog synths and horns are again essential, coloring a more metal-forward (oh, we’re beyond proto-metal now, babes) sound while also establishing these textures as something utterly integral to the UA sound, making them sound fuller and more complete and compelling than ever.The title track is a prime example, delivering that signature UA haunted bounce, recalling one of my all-time faves from Mind Control, “Poison Apple,” here with synths lending a cosmic warmth akin to Zombi that significantly ups the ante on the spooky factor. This fuller, more robust sound enhances their more metallic edge on this go, even with some Thin Lizzy-esque harmonies and more nuanced, detailed songwriting. Still catchy as all get-out, thankfully, but structurally, Shapes Of Midnight has way more meat on its bones, earning every second on the record’s longer compositions. The melodies, while a strong point on previous records, are at full-tilt here in many forms. B-side opener “Psycho on the Loose” delivers a well-timed 80s metal gut- punch in the vein of Judas Priest with one of the best hooks of their entire discography. Similarly, “Don’t Let It Control You” finds a surfy, classic rock ‘n’ roll backbone where keys bang away, and yet again, the way things come together feels so right, not homage-y, schtick-y, or experimental, but rather that UA is just dripping in such rich horror and throwback atmosphere that the juxtaposition of these tracks doesn’t even make me flinch.The pieces they've put into motion and the world they’ve built over the last couple records feels like it’s fully realized here. “When Evil Wakes” gives the synths and horns even more room to shine, hitting this sort of Doors-y stride, even dipping toes in a pitch-black boogie before gathering steam and building to a Sabotage-era Black Sabbath peak where leads flirt and dance around one another, richly layered vocals froth up a hypnotic haze, acoustic guitars lend a metallic ring, and the bass and drums lock into a groove both nimble and rock solid. It’s an early highlight representative of their comfort, confidence, and vision. “The Other Side of the Sky” connects with another stellar metal hook, matching this buzzy, near-sci-fi synth with a cowbell-laden stomp that will satisfy Mountain fans. Bigger yet is “I Won’t Sleep (‘til You’re Gone)” which captures glam and psychedelia through a veil of sepia-tinged goth rock, boasting bombasts of horns that are as infectious as they are curious—it’s almost surprising there’s not an Iggy Pop guest spot on this track. It’s sassy, sultry, and downright chilling. (“We’ll be turning the soil while your bones start to boil on the stove”? Oof!) Again, the production is phenomenal, every element hits with clarity, power, and purpose. Truly and expertly orchestrated.Ultimately, Shapes Of Midnight offers a complete, well-rounded, and fully actualized version of the Uncle Acid we’ve all …kind of… heard before. The retro flavors are absolutely on point with the additional instrumentation, the songwriting is as sharp as ever, and the horror storytelling inspired by Poe’s The Masque of the Red Death offers depth and intrigue. It’s exactly what I didn’t know I had been waiting for, and by the time the oddly bluesy, almost Danzig-esque closer “Sleep No More” drives its artful and unnerving final nail in the coffin, Shapes Of Midnight has revealed itself as not just a fantastic record in its own right, but also as the culmination of years of harrowing work. (Un)Safe to say, the time to reconnect with your old Uncle Acid has never been better.

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Fleesh is a duo of young Brazilian musicians formed in 2014 by Celo Oliveira, a highly skilled multi-instrumentalist (on guitar, he can tackle any style with equal success, and his electric guitar solos are particularly well-crafted), and Gabby Vessoni, a singer with a very captivating voice. I have absolutely nothing against female progressive rock singers. Quite the contrary. There are even times when that's practically all I listen to. But a pretty, expressive voice with character?whether soft or energetic?isn't enough for me. Above all, I need music that inspires and moves me. That's the case with Fleesh, whom I discovered on YouTube through their numerous videos of flawless covers of prog giants?Rush, Renaissance, Genesis, and Marillion foremost among them. The duo has dedicated entire tribute albums to each of them, including the 2020 double album *In The Mist Of Time* for Renaissance (covering "Song of Scheherazade," "Can You Understand?" and "Ashes Are Burning"?talk about daring!). Some covers are even better than the originals (check out their version of BJH's "Play to the World" online), and Gabby Vessoni's vocals on the Renaissance tracks almost make you forget Annie Haslam's?and it's no sacrilege to say so. Listen to "Golden Keys" to see for yourself.Celo Oliveira is magnificent, no matter the band he covers, the genre he explores, or the instrument he plays, and Gabby Vessoni is a queen?probably the singer I wouldn't hesitate to rank above all others, my favorite ever since Annie Haslam has taken a back seat and Kate Bush (in a radically different style, I admit) seems to have left us for good. Yet they don't seem to be very well-known or in high demand. One appears in the background on the superb opening track of *Abandoned*, the album by the Canadian band Huis; and the other was a member of Lyria, a Brazilian metal band. And beyond her cover videos?which are highly popular among internet users?Fleesh's fame is far from overwhelming, not to say very limited, and that's a real shame. Let's make a modest attempt to remedy this regrettable oversight. Fleesh's third album, *Across the Sea*, released in 2019, might help us do just that. With a mid-tempo style that borrows heavily from Anathema, Marillion, Pink Floyd, and Mostly Autumn, it contains a few gems that stand out from the crowd, such as the title track (a subtle tribute to Genesis's "Ripples"), the slow waltz of "Weight of the World," and especially "Whispers," which showcases all of Gabby's evocative power when she lets loose.But it's above all the new album *Eclipsed* that stands out, going further than its predecessors to ultimately distance itself even more from its initial influences and showcase a strong sense of identity?something "Stuck" proudly declares right from the start of the album, an impression reinforced by the superb video accompanying this potential hit online (if the word "hit" still holds any meaning, especially in progressive rock). And how can one remain unmoved by the heart-wrenching "Pile Of Bones," which is also accompanied by an original video directed by Gabby herself? For an hour, Fleesh delivers even more energy and bite than before, as heard in the title track, "No Rewind"?which evokes the Rush of the '90s?and "One By One," with its unexpected breaks and shifts in rhythm. "Down Below" is another standout moment, with more prominent keyboard work and an unstoppable melody reminiscent of Mostly Autumn at their best. And crowning it all is "All My Sins" (5:06), the quintessence of the duo at their peak. Gabby's restrained yet powerful delivery toward the end of this devastating waltz is hard to describe but plays a major role in making *Eclipsed* as thrilling as it is essential

items.body: Review by ZowieZiggy — Yet another review for a Purple live album.But I still enjoy to listen and review such sort of record.My first live encounter dated from March, 1973 in Brussels. (Belgium). I was 14 years old...And the ladst one will be on October 20. 2026, in Madrid (Spain). Quite a long ride isn't it?This double CD starts with 2 killers: "Highway Star" & "Black Night".Difficult to imagine a better start! And the so afraid "karaokee" style is even forgotten during the latter. So far, so great!Two very good renditions of � tracks from "The Battle Rages On" (logical since it was released in 1993 (date of recording of this live set).then come a superb "Bethoven's Ninth"...the magic of Jon to combine classic with rock; A somptuous 10 minutes (or almost) track which brings me close to ectasy (at times!). To confirm the great shape, the great "Knocking on your Back Door" from "Perfect Strangers" adds to the general feeling. SUPERB!!!But, what to say write about the two pieces of resistance of this double CD set???"Child in Time" (from "In Rock") and the fabulous, and the best from all their live sets for "Anya".This closes CD1 that be rated as a 5* one.CD2 though will sound a little weaker.Not with "The Battle" nor "lazy" which are outstanding as well. But thereafter, the next 3 titels are shortered versions of known numbers just as on their "NEC" live. Press next. three tiems;Then, we are going to face an EXTRAordinary cover version of a mythical Stones song. My favorite of tyhis great rock band. "Paint it, Blcack". from hard rocking to spacey: it is soooo great. One of the too few highlights of disc 2.We're back on great track with "Speed King" (we can even hear some notes from "Burn" before minute 6 (only instrumental, 'cause Ian will NEVER sing sing it; nor any song from Mark 3.The last but one song is an OK version of "Hush" from Mark I...But the worse is goi,ng to happen to the overlooooong karaoke version of "Smoke on the Water".I really couldn't stand this while attending their concerts. What I did at the time, was going up to the floors and attend the bar to drink one (or two - remember, I'm Belgian) with one of my mates (hi, Jean-Pierre). It was in the Arena in Antwerp (just next door to the Sport Palace).The intro is fine (almost 3 minutes) is fine with me; As well as the core track...which leads us to minute 7.And then ...5 minutes of Smoooooooke on the Water...for about another 3 minutes.The audience might have loved this, but I didn't...Sorry guys...All in all, this is an excellent hard-rocking live album. Another one from Purple; THE MASTER, THE INVENTER of the genre.**** solid stars. .

items.body: Ministry released its eleventh studio album, “The Last Sucker”, on 18 September 2007 through 13th Planet Records. The album turns 19 this year. MusicBrainz lists a first-release date of 8 September 2007, while Wikipedia and Discogs both confirm 18 September 2007 for the US release; Side-Line marks the anniversary on the date corroborated by the two independent sources. Al Jourgensen and Dave Donnelly produced the album, recorded in May 2007 at 13th Planet Studios in El Paso, Texas, with John Bilberry engineering and Donnelly also handling mastering. “The Last Sucker” closed the trilogy of anti-George W. Bush albums that began with “Houses of the Molé” (2004) and continued with “Rio Grande Blood” (2006). Jourgensen told Billboard at the time that he intended it to be Ministry’s final album, joking he would rather “leave on top of my game” than keep recording into old age; the band did not release another studio album of new material until “Relapse” in 2012. What is on Ministry’s ‘The Last Sucker’ The album runs 11 tracks: “Let’s Go”, “Watch Yourself”, “Life Is Good”, “The Dick Song”, “The Last Sucker”, “No Glory”, “Death & Destruction”, “Roadhouse Blues” (a cover of The Doors), “Die in a Crash”, “End of Days (Pt. 1)” and “End of Days (Pt. 2)”, with a total running time of 55:58. Deluxe and promotional editions added remixes of “Watch Yourself”, “The Last Sucker”, “Die in a Crash”, “No Glory” and “Death & Destruction” as bonus tracks. Fear Factory frontman Burton C. Bell provided guest lead vocals on “Die in a Crash” and both parts of “End of Days”. Paul Raven, formerly of Killing Joke, played bass and guitar and contributed backing vocals on several tracks; Prong and Danzig guitarist Tommy Victor played guitars and bass throughout. Sin Quirin and keyboardist John Bechdel also performed on the album. Closing track “End of Days (Pt. 2)” samples Dwight D. Eisenhower’s 1961 farewell address on the military-industrial complex alongside a reprise of “O Fortuna”, which had opened “Houses of the Molé” at the start of the trilogy. About Ministry Ministry formed in Chicago in 1981, led by vocalist, multi-instrumentalist and producer Al Jourgensen, the band’s sole constant member. The debut album, “With Sympathy”, released through Arista in 1983 in a synth-pop style Jourgensen later disowned, was followed by a move toward industrial rock on Sire/Warner Bros. releases including “Twitch” (1986), “The Land of Rape and Honey” (1988) and “The Mind Is a Terrible Thing to Taste” (1989). “Psalm 69: The Way to Succeed and the Way to Suck Eggs” (1992) became the band’s commercial peak, reaching number 27 on the Billboard 200 and going platinum on the strength of “Jesus Built My Hotrod” and “N.W.O.”. After “Filth Pig” (1996) and “Dark Side of the Spoon” (1999), Ministry signed to Sanctuary and released “Animositisomina” (2003) before launching its own label, 13th Planet Records, with “Houses of the Molé” (2004), the first instalment of the anti-Bush trilogy that continued with “Rio Grande Blood” (2006) and closed with “The Last Sucker” (2007). Bassist Paul Raven died in October 2007, shortly after the album’s release. Jourgensen revived Ministry for “Relapse” (2012) and Ministry’s ‘From Beer to Eternity’ turns 13 on 6 September (2013), the latter completed following guitarist Mike Scaccia’s death during recording. Ministry has continued releasing albums on Nuclear Blast, including “AmeriKKKant” (2018), “Moral Hygiene” (2021) and “Hopiumforthemasses” (2024).
items._cn_summary: 本文为Side-Line杂志发布的专辑纪念性资讯文章，介绍Ministry第十一张录音室专辑《The Last Sucker》的发行信息。该专辑于2007年发行，是Al Jourgensen反布什三部曲的终章（前两部分别为2004年的《Houses of the Molé》和2006年的《Rio Grande Blood》）。专辑共收录11首曲目，总时长55分58秒，制作人为Jourgensen与Dave Donnelly，于德州El Paso的13th Planet Studios录制。Fear Factory主唱Burton C. Bell在《Die in a Crash》及《End of Days》两部中担任客串主唱，Killing Joke前成员Paul Raven、Prong和Danzig的Tommy Victor等亦参与演奏。终曲采样了艾森豪威尔1961年告别演说中关于军工复合体的段落，并以《O Fortuna》的再现呼应三部曲的开篇。文章本身为新闻式回顾，缺乏对音乐文本的深入分析。

items.body: Shostakovich was thirty when he wrote his Symphony No. 5 in 1937, the year after the Communist Party newspaper Pravda attacked his opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District. His Fourth Symphony had been withdrawn during rehearsals, announced as his own decision, though the pressure behind it is well documented. The Fifth’s Leningrad premiere under Yevgeny Mravinsky drew a long ovation and restored his position with the authorities. In the press the symphony was soon called a Soviet artist’s creative reply to just criticism, a line the composer never wrote but never disowned. The scoring is for a large orchestra with piano, celesta, harps and a full percussion section. Four movements run from a broad Moderato to a fast finale, by way of a short scherzo and a Largo that leaves the brass silent. The strings begin the work alone with a wide-leaping figure, and the finale turns its D minor into a loud D major. Whether that ending is genuine triumph or forced rejoicing has been argued for decades, and the second reading rests largely on Testimony, a memoir of disputed authenticity. Conductors answer the question in performance, above all in how fast they take the coda. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the 10 best recordings of Shostakovich’s Symphony No. 5. Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra, Yevgeny Mravinsky Mravinsky gave the first performance of the Fifth in 1937, and this concert recording, made forty-six years later, is his last word on it. Age had taken nothing from his hold on the score. The playing is fierce, and the shape of each movement stays clear under pressure. The finale sets off at a speed that sounds dangerous, then broadens at the close into something implacable. He pays no attention to the tempo mark printed at that point, and the ending is stronger for it. The orchestra is not always immaculate and a cough or two carries from the hall, but nothing else here has quite this authority. Mravinsky Amazon Presto New York Philharmonic, Leonard Bernstein Played as a virtuoso showpiece, the symphony gains a thrill it loses in graver hands. Bernstein had conducted it in the Soviet Union weeks earlier, with the composer in the hall and delighted by what he heard. This recording followed at home that October. The finale is the fastest here by a distance, and it takes the closing pages as plain triumph, with no hint that the rejoicing is forced. That choice divides listeners, and some find four movements at this pitch exhausting. For anyone who wants the ending to sound like a victory, this is the one. Bernstein Amazon Presto Apple London Symphony Orchestra, André Previn Refinement and drive rarely sit together in this symphony, but Previn found both in 1965 with the London Symphony Orchestra. The playing is rich and full, and nothing sounds rushed even where the tempos are quick. He puts his weight on the slow movement, which he lets stretch out and takes down to a whisper. The scherzo is the other high point, with the cellos and basses biting into the dance. His finale runs close to the speed printed in the score, nearer Bernstein than the slower modern versions. The transfer has its costs. Climaxes are a little flattened and rumble is audible in parts of the first movement, yet this is still one of the finest accounts of its era. Previn Amazon Presto Apple Berlin Symphony Orchestra, Kurt Sanderling Hearing this 1982 recording after the others is like having the score opened out on the table. Sanderling was in the hall for a Moscow performance weeks after the premiere, and in 1949 he conducted the concert that brought the work back into Soviet programs. What he offers is not weight or theater but clarity. The first movement is measured, the loud passages are scaled so that nothing is buried, and inner parts that usually pass unnoticed come through. High strings can sound a little glassy at the top, a small price for a reading that feels closer than any other here to the man who wrote the symphony. Sanderling Amazon Presto Apple Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Bernard Haitink Steadiness rather than terror is what Haitink offers in this 1981 recording. The orchestra is superb, the recorded sound warm and open, and the opening movement lands with real impact. What Haitink withholds is menace. The manner stays level where others press harder, the woodwind entries in the slow movement could be sharper, and the coda is finely judged where others are defiant. Some listeners want more horror from this symphony than they will find here. As orchestral playing, though, it is hard to beat. Haitink Amazon Presto Apple Royal Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra, Vasily Petrenko Everything in Petrenko’s 2008 account is shaped by what happens at the end, and what happens at the end is a refusal to celebrate. He travels between extremes of loud and soft that few others attempt, and the detail he uncovers on the way is remarkable. The last movement holds a central stretch full of regret before the coda arrives at a crawl, closer to defiance than to victory. It is a hard listen by design, and not everyone will want the symphony to end this way. A few of his tempo shifts sound deliberate where they should feel inevitable, but nothing here states the case for the hollow ending more powerfully. Petrenko Amazon Presto Apple Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra, Manfred Honeck Take the dynamic and balance markings literally, as Honeck does in this 2013 concert recording, and the symphony changes character. Details that normally sink into the texture come through clearly: the harp in the first movement, the piano at the climax of the Largo. Neither is a discovery, since both are in the score, but they are seldom this audible. The slow movement is the peak here, carried with dignity and a kind of quiet grief, never pressed for effect. He takes his time throughout, and the scherzo loses some of its irony as a result. Few recordings, though, let you hear so much of what is actually on the page. Honeck Amazon Presto Apple Boston Symphony Orchestra, Andris Nelsons The Boston Symphony Orchestra plays magnificently here, with trumpets that would be hard to better in any recent recording of this music. Nelsons keeps a current of unease running from the opening bars, and it never quite lets up, even in the passages that offer relief. One of those comes midway through the first movement, where the flute and horn answer each other over the strings and the music opens out for a moment. The sound is spacious, though there is a shade too much reverberation at the start for the string playing to register cleanly. No modern version sounds bigger, a broad canvas where Petrenko is lean. Nelsons Amazon Presto Apple London Symphony Orchestra, Maxim Shostakovich Maxim Shostakovich takes the symphony more slowly than anyone else here, well over ten minutes longer than Mravinsky across the four movements. The pulse never sags, which is what makes the approach work. The London Symphony Orchestra plays with complete seriousness. His slow movement refuses to plead. Feeling is held back instead of displayed, and the restraint is what makes it land. The finale’s march moves at a pace that cannot be hurried, with a central episode where real warmth breaks through, and its scale becomes the argument. Maxim Shostakovich Amazon Presto Apple Moscow Philharmonic Orchestra, Kirill Kondrashin By 1964 the symphony was nearly thirty years old, but this recording catches it as though the ink were still wet. Kondrashin, who gave the premieres of two of the composer’s symphonies and recorded the first complete cycle, drives the outer movements harder and rougher than almost any rival. Polish is not the point. Urgency is, and the coda in particular lands with a force smoother versions never find. The engineering shows its age, and this is not always the first Fifth recommended from his cycle. For anyone who wants the symphony at its most dangerous, it is still the obvious choice. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了肖斯塔科维奇《第五交响曲》的十个经典录音版本，乐评聚焦于该作品的历史背景与指挥诠释。作品创作于1937年，正值作曲家因歌剧《姆钦斯克县的麦克白夫人》受到《真理报》批判之后，列宁格勒首演在穆拉文斯基指挥下获得巨大成功，帮助作曲家重新获得官方认可。乐评讨论了终乐章D小调转D大调的解读争议，以及指挥通过尾声速度处理来回答这一问题的不同方式。三位指挥的录音被详细评述：穆拉文斯基的现场版本展现权威与力度，伯恩斯坦以最快速的处理呈现纯粹的胜利感，普雷文则强调精致与张力的平衡，慢乐章被延伸至低语般的尾声。文章属于传统古典音乐评论范畴，与实验、前卫或电子音乐等偏好方向相距较远。

今年は、戦後日本を代表する作曲家でありながら46歳で夭逝した矢代秋雄（1929～1976）の没後50年にあたる。 「音楽の友」2026年10月号では、特別企画として生前に交流のあった音楽家と、近年その演奏が話題となった演奏家が矢代について語っている。ここでは、そのなかから印象的なことばを紹介する。 1968年、同級生である黛敏郎（右）と 矢代秋雄（やしろ・あきお 1929年9月10日―1976年4月9日） 1929年、東京生まれ。東京音楽学校研究科修了。1951年から1956年まで、フランス政府給費留学生としてパリ国立高等音楽院に留学し、ナディア・ブーランジェ、ジャック・ドゥ・ラ・プレール、オリヴィエ・メシアンらに師事。その後、東京藝術大学作曲科教授を務め、後進の指導にもあたりました。1976年、46歳で急逝。 生前に交流のあった音楽家のことば 野平一郎 ～東京藝術大学の教員だった矢代に学生として接した作曲家 その手触りはゴツゴツしていて、「フランス派」とかいう馬鹿馬鹿しいレッテルが想像させるような、滑らかなものではけっしてなかった。 原文では、矢代が46歳で早世したときに東京藝大の4年生だった筆者が、当時の衝撃や仕事ぶりを振り返る。「時代は矢代秋雄に追いついたか」と題して綴られた、作品についての論考も必読だ。（文＝野平一郎） 青柳いづみこ ～矢代から直接指導を受けたピアニスト・文筆家 フランス仕込みのアカデミックな作風で知られるが、作品には日本的な要素も多く盛り込まれている。 10月18日（日）に開催される、矢代の没後50年記念コンサートの曲目について、矢代の遺した言葉を用いながら聴きどころを解説。（文＝青柳いづみこ） 青柳いづみこさん企画・構成 矢代秋雄 没後50年記念コンサート 日時： 10月18日（日）14時開演 会場： 浜離宮朝日ホール 出演： 青柳いづみこ（企画・構成・ピアノ・お話） 田所光之マルセル（ピアノ） 多久和怜子・占部智美（フルート） プログラム： ピアノのためのソナチネ（1945）（青柳） ピアノ連弾のための古典組曲（1951）（田所・青柳） 2本のフルートとピアノのためのソナタ（1958）（多久和・占部・青柳） ノクチュルヌ（夜曲）（1947） （青柳） ミニ・レクチャー（お話：青柳） 矢代秋雄のソナタとベートーヴェン「ソナタop.109」 ピアノ・ソナタ（1961） （田所） チケット申し込み： 朝日ホール・チケットセンター Tel. 03-3267-9990（日・祝除く10:00～18:00） https://www.asahi-hall.jp/hamarikyu/ticket/ 問い合わせ： 音楽之友社楽譜部 Tel. 03-3235-2135 近年演奏が話題となった演奏家 山田和樹 ～N響やバーミンガム市響で矢代作品を指揮して 「交響曲」は自筆譜で演奏させていただいたのですが、その筆致をよく見てみると、一音一音にすごく確信がある。 最初に指揮した矢代作品である「ピアノ協奏曲」（演奏：NHK交響楽団／ピアノ：河村尚子）や、昨年バーミンガム市響と「交響曲」を演奏したときのエピソードを交えて、矢代作品のオリジナリティについて語っている。（取材・文＝西村祐） 河村尚子 ～「ピアノ協奏曲」を二度演奏して ご自身がピアノの名手であったこともあり、「ピアノ協奏曲」でもピアニストに要求されるものがとても大きいのです。（中略）たくさんの音色を描いていかなければならない。 「ピアノ協奏曲」を指揮者の下野竜也さん、山田和樹さんと共演して以来、「ピアノ・ソナタ」や小品にも取り組むようになった河村さん。「ピアノ協奏曲」においては、繊細さをきわめるような情景から、暴力的でアグレッシヴなシーンまで、常に音色を変化させていかなければならない。その多彩さこそが矢代作品の特徴のひとつだという。 上村文乃 ～2025年に初演者だった堤剛さんの代奏をして （チェロ協奏曲は）チェロのレチタティーヴォ（朗唱）と歌が非常に印象的です。（中略）オリエンタルな空気を感じつつ、西洋的な美や趣きがあるように感じられます。 日本に勢いのあった1960年に作曲された「チェロ協奏曲」。その時代性へ思いを寄せ、矢代と同級生である黛敏郎の無伴奏チェロ作品《BUNRAKU》を引き合いに出しながら、作品の魅力や音のつくりかたの細部などに言及している。   堤剛さんの弾く「チェロ協奏曲」が収録されたアルバム 矢代秋雄の関連本 「音楽の友」2026年10月号（9月18日発売）。特別企画として「没後50年記念 矢代秋雄の世界」を掲載 飾らず率直に綴られた、みずみずしい息吹を味わえる矢代秋雄の名エッセイ集 矢代秋雄 特設ページ 関連記事「ヨーロッパとのはてしない距離──矢代秋雄の孤独」

items._cn_summary: 本文围绕日本战后作曲家矢代秋雄没后五十周年纪念活动展开，属于杂志专题预告性质的内容，并非完整乐评。文章介绍了矢代的生平和留法经历，汇集了多位音乐家与演奏家的简短访谈片段，包括作曲家野平一郎、钢琴家青柳いづみこ与河村尚子、指挥家山田和樹、大提琴家上村文乃，分别谈及矢代作品的触感、东西方融合特征、钢琴协奏曲的多彩音色要求以及六十年代日本现代音乐语境下创作的《チェロ協奏曲》。文章附有纪念音乐会的曲目和票务信息。整体偏重资料性介绍，对作品风格与手法的分析浅尝辄止，信息密度和评论深度有限。

ニューヨークのクラシック音楽エージェント、エンタテインメント会社勤務を経て、クラシック音楽を中心としたパフォーミング・アーツ全般について執筆、日本の戯曲の英訳も手掛け... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る ウクライナ・フリーダム・オーケストラが8月25日と26日、リンカーン・センターのデイヴィッド・ゲフェン・ホールで演奏会を行った。同団は、ウクライナ国内のオーケストラ所属メンバーやウクライナ国外に逃れた音楽家らをメンバーとして、ロシアのウクライナ侵攻に対する反応として、2022年にウクライナ系カナダ人指揮者、ケリー＝リン・ウィルソンによって結成された。 以来、ウクライナの文化とレジリエンスを世界に示し、犠牲者を追悼するとともに平和を訴えることを目的とするという同団は、夏のオフシーズンを中心に活動を続けている。いまだに停戦の明確な兆しは見出されないなか、この8月に行われた欧米ツアーには、「2026年インヴィンシブル（無敵）・ツアー」と、かなり直接的な名称が与えられている。 設立当初から同団には広報から芸術面までメトロポリタン歌劇場（MET）が深くかかわっており、METは昨シーズンの公演プログラム冊子にも、毎回ウクライナ支持のメッセージを掲載した。ポーランド国立歌劇場やウクライナ文化省も協力し、2023年以来、ウクライナ大統領夫人オレナ・ゼレンスカの後援を得ているという。 そのような背景を意識せずとも、民族的なつながりが感じられるメンバーの顔、演奏が終わったあとに抱き合ってお互いを讃えあう姿などに、このアンサンブルの成り立ちが特殊であり、特別であることが感じられる。 はたしてウィルソン率いる同団の演奏は、一糸乱れぬアンサンブルというわけではないものの、全体として柔軟なつながりで聴かせる魅力的なものだった。 ウィルソンはニューヨーク・フィルハーモニックからNHK交響楽団まで、すでにさまざまなオーケストラとシンフォニー指揮者としての経験を積んでいるが、少なくともニューヨークでは、これまでオペラ指揮者としての印象のほうが強かったように思う。 しかし25日に演奏されたベートーヴェン「交響曲第7番」では、同曲のような人気交響曲でも豊かな音色を聴かせるダイナミックな統率力が印象的だった。最終楽章は現代の演奏らしく猛烈に速いテンポだが、疾走感が持続して息切れするところがなく、爽快だ。 もっとも8月25日の最大の呼び物は、休憩前に演奏されたリーゼ・ダーヴィドセンがソリストのR.シュトラウス《4つの最後の歌》であった。今回のツアーはヨーロッパ5都市とニューヨークを回るものだったが、ヨーロッパ5都市ではダーヴィドセンは登場せず、曲も別のものとなっている。彼女の登場が実現したのは、彼女とMETのつながりが深いことに加え、9月のシーズン初日にヴェルディ《マクベス》でマクベス夫人を歌うため、たまたまニューヨークに滞在していたためと思われる。 ダーヴィドセンの歌は、言葉一つひとつのニュアンスを枝葉末節にこだわって抽出するより、真正面からたゆたうように聴かせる。その現代随一の声の力があってこその表現であり、年齢を重ねることによる解釈の深まりを予感させる余裕も感じさせてくれた。ウィルソンの指揮も、そんなダーヴィドセンの現在の美点を支える推進力のあるものだった。 ウクライナ・フリーダム・オーケストラのヴェルディ「レクイエム」から（8月26日、デイヴィッド・ゲフェン・ホール）© Richard Termine / Met Opera 8月26日にはヴェルディ「レクイエム」が演奏された。ここでは何よりも、METの合唱団メンバーによって構成されたMETコーラス・アーティスツの好演が印象的で、冒頭から最後まで緊張感を保ちながらも柔らかに深く響いた合唱は、この日最大の立役者であった。 METの中堅的存在であるアイリーン・ペレス（S）とソロマン・ハワード（Bs）に加え、ナタリー・ルイス（Ms）、ルネ・バルベラ（T）らソリストの歌唱も安定感のあるもので、とりわけペレスの声と歌唱は、現在のMETの水準を表すものとして興味深いものだった。 ウィルソンの指揮も、よく指摘されるこの曲のオペラ的なダイナミックさを抽出したものだった。そしてそのダイナミックさは、現代の戦争に対する恐怖と怒りにふさわしく感じられるもので、全体を鎮魂曲としてインスパイアされるものにしていた。 ちなみに両日とも冒頭にはウクライナ人作曲家の作品が演奏され、25日はマクシム・コロミレツ（1981年生まれ）の《The Mothers of Kherson》（ヘルソンの母たち）からの組曲が、26日にはボフダナ・フロリャク（1968年生まれ）の《グローリア》が演奏された。そしてアンコールとして最後には、弦楽曲として編曲されたウクライナ国歌が美しく演奏された。
items._cn_summary: 本文报道乌克兰自由管弦乐团在纽约林肯中心的两场演出。该乐团由乌克兰系加拿大人指挥凯莉-林·威尔逊于2022年组建，旨在战乱中弘扬乌克兰文化并呼吁和平。两晚分别演奏贝多芬第七交响曲与理查·施特劳斯《最后四首歌》（由女高音达维德森担任独唱），以及威尔第《安魂曲》，曲目前后分别上演乌克兰当代作曲家作品如《赫尔森母亲》组曲与《光荣》，终曲为乌克兰国歌弦乐改编版。评论侧重于指挥风格的动态控制、独唱家的声线表现及MET合唱团的张力营造，与实验性音乐语境关联薄弱。

items.body: [PLAYLIST] Kurator Mike Patricola und das Label Smiling C – das Team hinter Voice of Love – sind zurück. Pipe Dreams heißt die neue Compilation, die am 23. Oktober erscheinen wird. Sie enthält 19 vergessene Songs, aufgenommen zwischen Ende der 1970er und Mitte der 1980er, die – nun ja – nah am Wasser gebaut sind. Wortwörtlich. Seite A klassischer Yacht Rock, Seite B Surf-Disco, Seite C zeigt intimere »tropische Troubadoure«, Seite D schließt die Klammer mit Yacht-Rock. Not Only Surfin‘ U.S.A Die versammelten Interpret:innen kommen nicht nur aus den USA, sondern auch aus Australien, Japan, Kanada, Frankreich, von den Bahamas oder von Hawaii. Die Compilation zeigt Yacht Rock nicht als eine auf Kalifornien begrenzte, sondern als globale Ästhetik. Der Japaner Twin Cosmos legt auf »Coconuts Wind« eine Lennon erinnernde Melodie in eine lauwarme Meeresbrise. Pierre Rochette aus Montréal träumt sich mit afrikanischen Rhythmen und Disco-Gitarren-Grooves »On The Beach«. Miles Corbin Rick Sharp Twin Cosmos Die auf schwarzem Vinyl gepresste Schallplatte erscheint in einem luxuriösen, gestanzten Gatefold-Cover mit Spotlackierung und ist auf dem europäischen Festland exklusiv bei HHV erhältlich. Das Artwork stammt von Charles Bals und basiert auf dem Foto »Breaking Wave« von Lex Thompson. Im HHV Shop kaufenV.A.Pipe Dreams HHV EU Exclusive Black Vinyl Editionab 47.99€
items._genre: yacht rock / soft rock / disco / compilation
items._cn_summary: 这是Smiling C厂牌策划的一张Yacht Rock主题合辑，收录了1970年代末至1980年代中期来自美国、澳大利亚、日本、加拿大、法国、巴哈马和夏威夷等地共19首被遗忘的作品。合辑以四面黑胶形式呈现，A面为经典Yacht Rock，B面为Surf-Disco，C面收录更具私密感的热带吟游曲目，D面回归Yacht Rock主题。曲目包括日本音乐人Twin Cosmos带有列侬式旋律的温柔创作，以及蒙特利尔的Pierre Rochette融合非洲节奏与迪斯科吉他律动的作品。该项目试图将Yacht Rock呈现为一种全球性的音乐美学，而非仅限于加州的地域风格。唱片采用镂空Gatefold封面配局部UV工艺，由欧洲独立渠道独家发行。整体为一张梳理与再发现性质的怀旧合辑。

items.excerpt: デラックス盤やアナログ・リイシューなどは続いていたものの、初出音源集は2021年の『 Welcome 2 America 』ぶり。デビュー前の77年に録音していた瑞々しいファンク“I Am You”から、2016年3月のピアノ弾き語りライヴ録音“How Come U Don’t Call Me Anymore?”まで約40年のキャリアから満遍なく未発表音源がチョイスされ、時代ごとの興味や志向の変化などを楽しむことができる。90年に世に出た“Tick, Tick, Bang”のニューウェイヴな初期ヴァージョン（81年）、ブートで人気だった名曲“I Wonder”（89年）、セリーヌ・ディオンに提供した“With This Tear”（91年）など聴きどころ多数!

items._cn_summary: 本文为Prince未发行音源合集《Timeless》的资讯性介绍，跨越约四十年创作生涯，从1977年早期录音到2016年钢琴弹唱现场均有收录。文章提及多首作品的版本演变与出处，包括81年录制的早期New Wave版本、89年曾流行于Bootleg的曲目，以及为Celine Dion创作的歌曲等。整体内容以信息罗列为主，属于遗作整理性质的发行，缺乏对音乐本体或艺术价值的深入评述。Prince的作品虽具一定个人色彩，但本文介绍的内容主要集中于流行、 funk、R&B等主流类型，与实验、前卫或即兴类音乐关联较弱，难以引起该用户群体的关注。

items.excerpt: マルチ楽器奏者でもあるシンガー・ソングライターが、猪爪東風プロデュースで親友のミュージシャンらと完成したEP。スティーヴィー・ワンダー由来なAOR風のJ-Popが小気味よく、KANとTENDREの中間とも言うべき絶妙な立ち位置。クラヴィネットとホーンが軽快な“Under the Surface”、〈未来予想図〉ならぬ、終わりを予感させるバラード“終末相関図”など、聴きどころは十分だ。

items._cn_summary: 志摩陽立以EP形式发行了由猪爪東風制作的六首作品，定位介于KAN与TENDRE之间的日本AOR风J-Pop。整体风格源自史蒂薇·汪达的黑色音乐传统，强调轻快的节奏与旋律性。编曲上以Clavinet与Horn为核心配置，作品“Under the Surface”展现轻快律动，“終末相関図”则是带有终结感的抒情慢板。制作依靠亲友乐手协力的录音室模式完成，音乐质地上偏向都市型软派灵魂流行，与实验、前卫、爵士即兴或电子领域几乎无交集，更接近主流成人抒情与流行融合的范畴。对偏好实验、前卫或地下声响的听众而言，这张作品信息密度与艺术冒险性均偏低。

items._cn_summary: 这是一档名为《Race The Sky》的电台节目播单，第026期由Cliff Furnald主持，时长涵盖90年间的各类音乐。节目策划风格相当混杂，艺人跨度极大：从经典人物David Bowie、Sophia Loren与Peter Sellers的合作、Cream乐队，到Seth Avett、Justin Adams、Mauro Duarte等当代艺人，再到来自冈比亚的Dawda Jobarteh、尼日利亚的Alhaji Waziri Oshomah等世界音乐领域的演奏者，以及DOGO、Issa Murad、Eneida Marta等较少被英语世界听众熟知的名字。整体编排呈现拼贴式选曲逻辑，缺乏明确的风格主线，每位艺人仅出现几分钟片段。内容本身并非原创乐评，而是电台节目的曲目预告与简介，文字极短，信息密度很低，难以据此判断其艺术质量与编辑意图。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John 1999年在德国洛雷莱露天剧场的演出，以四重奏编制演绎新奥尔良经典曲目。演出以Mardi Gras街头游行传统的'Iko Iko'开场，涵盖'Mac's神秘主义'色彩浓郁的'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'、Duke Ellington的'我要去钓鱼'以及Earl King的'Big Chief'等。整体呈现是新奥尔良R&B、funk与布鲁斯的传统融合，以钢琴为核心，结合吉他、贝斯和鼓的紧凑编制。文章还穿插介绍了洛雷莱作为联合国教科文组织世界遗产地的文化背景，以及Rockpalast作为西德广播电视台自1974年以来的音乐节目档案来源。乐评文字在末尾略显断裂，但内容主要聚焦于现场曲目回顾与场地文化语境。

items._cn_summary: 这是一档名为Racing into the Big Muddy的广播节目节目单，内容以民谣、根源音乐和世界音乐为主题，涵盖Dr. John、Johnny Cash、Paul Simon、Pete Seeger等主流民谣与蓝草艺人，同时收录了部分欧洲和非洲的世界音乐曲目如Maria Kalaniemi与Pekko K�ppi、Saly Kouyate等。节目以河流与沼泽为主题串联选曲，涉及乡村布鲁斯、美国民谣复兴、北欧民间音乐和西非传统等方向。整体内容偏向传统根源音乐和世界民谣的杂锦汇编，缺乏对实验性、前卫性或电子元素的探讨，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、自由爵士及电子方向相距较远。此外原文仅为节目曲目列表，不构成实质性乐评，信息量极为有限。
